01-26.sens: Paul entrusted Churches to them, Timothy at Ephesus and Titus in Crete, and wrote them letters that are in the Bible. Their feast follows that of Paul's conversion.
01-26.vivre: Give thanks for someone who has walked with you and trusted you.

01-27: Saint Angela Merici: an Italian woman who wanted girls to be educated, at a time when it was rarely done.

01-27.qui: Angela Merici (1474-1540), orphaned very young, lived in Brescia, in Italy.
01-27.sens: She founded the Company of Saint Ursula, consecrated women who lived in the world and taught girls: the Ursulines, who opened schools all over the world.
01-27.vivre: Teach a child something you know how to do.

01-28: Saint Thomas Aquinas: a towering thinker who said at the end that all he had written was like straw compared with God.

01-28.qui: Thomas Aquinas (1225-1274), an Italian Dominican, is one of the Church's greatest theologians.
01-28.sens: His work, the Summa Theologiae, explains the faith through reason. Shortly before his death, after an experience in prayer, he said that everything he had written seemed like straw compared with what he had seen. He is celebrated on 28 January, the day his relics were moved to Toulouse, where he rests.
01-28.vivre: Ask God, simply, a question you have about the faith.

01-29: A monk from Britain who came to Brittany and founded the abbey of Rhuys.

01-29.qui: Gildas (c. 500-570), a monk from Britain, settled in Brittany.
01-29.sens: He founded the abbey of Saint-Gildas-de-Rhuys and wrote a stern book about the misfortunes of his homeland. He is much venerated in Brittany.
01-29.vivre: Visit a place of prayer near where you live.

01-30: A Roman martyr, honoured as one of the patron saints of the city.

01-30.qui: According to tradition, Martina was a young martyr of Rome in the third century.
01-30.sens: Her relics, found in the seventeenth century, rest in the church of Saints Luke and Martina in the Roman Forum. She is one of the patron saints of Rome.
01-30.vivre: Pray for the Christians of Rome and for the Pope.

01-31: Saint John Bosco: the priest of Turin's street boys, who taught through joy and trust.

01-31.qui: John Bosco (1815-1888) was a priest in Turin, from a poor farming family.
01-31.sens: He took in boys from the streets and taught them a trade and the faith, through games, trust and joy. He founded the Salesians, now present in more than a hundred countries. He is the patron saint of educators and young people.
01-31.vivre: Play with a child properly, without looking at your phone.

02-01: Saint Brigid of Kildare: an Irish abbess famous for her generosity and hospitality.

02-01.qui: Brigid (c. 451-525) was an Irish abbess, founder of the monastery of Kildare.
02-01.sens: She is famous for her generosity: it is said she gave away whatever came to hand. With Saint Patrick she is the patron saint of Ireland, where crosses of woven rushes are made on this day.
02-01.vivre: Give something away on the spur of the moment.

02-02: Mary and Joseph bring Jesus to the Temple: this is Candlemas.

02-02.qui: Forty days after Christmas, Mary and Joseph present Jesus in the Temple in Jerusalem.
02-02.sens: The old man Simeon takes him in his arms and calls him “a light for the nations” (Lk 2:32). That is why candles are blessed: it is Candlemas, the feast of candles.
02-02.vivre: Light a candle and say Simeon's prayer.

02-03: A bishop from Armenia; throats are still blessed in his name today.

02-03.qui: Blaise was a bishop of Sebaste in Armenia, martyred in the fourth century.
02-03.sens: He is said to have saved a child choking on a fishbone. Ever since, on 3 February, the priest blesses throats by holding two crossed candles under the chin of the faithful.
02-03.vivre: Pray for someone who is ill.

02-04: According to tradition, the woman who wiped the face of Jesus on the way of the cross.

02-04.qui: According to tradition, Veronica was a woman of Jerusalem.
02-04.sens: As Jesus carried his cross, she wiped his face with a cloth on which his features are said to have remained. Her name recalls vera icon, “true image”. This is the sixth Station of the Cross.
02-04.vivre: Do something gentle for someone who is suffering.

02-05: A martyr of Sicily, patron saint of Catania and of those who suffer.

02-05.qui: Agatha was a young martyr of Catania, in Sicily, in the third century.
02-05.sens: She rejected the advances of a governor and endured terrible tortures. Patron saint of Catania, she is invoked against eruptions of Etna and against fire.
02-05.vivre: Pray for women who suffer violence.

02-06: Saint Paul Miki and companions: twenty-six Christians crucified at Nagasaki in 1597, singing.

02-06.qui: Paul Miki and twenty-five companions, Japanese and European priests, religious and lay people, were crucified at Nagasaki on 5 February 1597.
02-06.sens: Among them were three boys. Paul Miki, a Japanese Jesuit, forgave his executioners from the cross. The Church in Japan then lived in hiding for more than two centuries.
02-06.vivre: Pray for the Christians of Japan.

02-07: Blessed Mary of Providence: born in Lille, she founded a congregation to pray for the dead and serve the living.

02-07.qui: Eugénie Smet (1825-1871), born in Lille, took the name Mary of Providence.
02-07.sens: In Paris she founded the Helpers of the Holy Souls, who pray for the dead and serve the sick and the poor. She was declared blessed in 1957.

02-08: Saint Josephine Bakhita: kidnapped as a child in Sudan and sold as a slave, she became a nun in Italy.

02-08.qui: Josephine Bakhita (c. 1869-1947) was kidnapped as a child in Sudan and sold several times as a slave.
02-08.sens: In Italy she discovered the faith, won her freedom and became a nun. She was canonized in 2000. 8 February is the World Day of Prayer against Human Trafficking.

02-09: A martyr of Alexandria, patron saint of dentists.

02-09.qui: Apollonia was an elderly deaconess of Alexandria, martyred in 249.
02-09.sens: During a riot against Christians, her teeth were broken before she was threatened with fire. She became the patron saint of dentists.
02-09.vivre: Pray for those who care for us, your dentist included.

02-10: Saint Benedict's twin sister, whose prayer brought on a storm.

02-10.qui: Scholastica (c. 480-543) was the twin sister of Saint Benedict.
02-10.sens: According to Saint Gregory the Great, on their last visit she begged her brother to stay and talk about God; he refused, she prayed, and a storm broke that kept him from leaving. Gregory concludes that she won, because she loved more.
02-10.vivre: Spend real time with a brother, sister or someone close.

02-11: On 11 February 1858, Mary appeared to Bernadette. It is also the World Day of the Sick.

02-11.qui: On 11 February 1858, in Lourdes, fourteen-year-old Bernadette Soubirous saw a “beautiful lady” in the grotto of Massabielle.
02-11.sens: She saw her eighteen times; the lady called herself “the Immaculate Conception”. Lourdes has become one of the largest shrines in the world. Since 1993 this has been the World Day of the Sick.
02-11.vivre: Pray for someone who is ill, or visit them.

02-12: Saint Bernard's sister, who left a worldly life to become a nun.

02-12.qui: Humbeline (1092-c. 1141) was the only sister of Saint Bernard of Clairvaux; her father and six brothers all became monks.
02-12.sens: Married to a nobleman, she lived in luxury. One day she came to see Bernard with a grand retinue; he refused to receive her. Touched, she changed her life and eventually entered the monastery of Jully in Burgundy, where she became prioress.
02-12.vivre: Accept a remark that helps you grow.

02-13: Saint Gilbert of Meaux: a bishop of Meaux a thousand years ago.

02-13.qui: Gilbert (c. 950-1009), born in Vermandois, was a canon at Saint-Quentin and then bishop of Meaux.
02-13.sens: Little is known about him, except that he supported the abbeys of his region. He is venerated in Meaux, where he died.
02-13.vivre: Think of the bishops and priests of your diocese.

02-14: Two brothers who invented an alphabet to give the Bible to the Slavic peoples.

02-14.qui: Cyril (827-869) and Methodius (c. 815-885), two brothers from Thessalonica, set out to bring the Gospel to the Slavic peoples.
02-14.sens: They invented an alphabet to translate the Bible and the liturgy into their language. John Paul II proclaimed them patrons of Europe. 14 February is also Saint Valentine's Day, a Roman martyr who became the patron of lovers.
02-14.vivre: Say thank you to the person you love.

02-15: Saint Claude de la Colombière: a Jesuit, friend and support of Saint Margaret Mary at Paray-le-Monial.

02-15.qui: Claude de la Colombière (1641-1682) was a French Jesuit.
02-15.sens: Sent to Paray-le-Monial, he became Margaret Mary Alacoque's confessor and supported her when no one believed her. He did much to spread devotion to the Heart of Jesus.
02-15.vivre: Listen to someone right to the end without judging.

02-16: A martyr of Nicomedia, in today's Turkey, in the early fourth century.

02-16.qui: Juliana was a young martyr of Nicomedia, in today's Turkey, in the early fourth century.
02-16.sens: According to tradition, she refused to marry a pagan and stayed faithful to Christ despite threats.
02-16.vivre: Pray for those facing a difficult choice.

02-17: The Seven Holy Founders of the Servites
Seven merchants of Florence who left everything to serve Mary.

02-17.qui: The Seven Holy Founders were seven merchants of Florence who, in 1233, left everything to live together in prayer.
02-17.sens: They founded the Order of the Servants of Mary, devoted to Our Lady of Sorrows. The youngest, Alexis Falconieri, lived to 110 according to tradition.
02-17.vivre: Pray with Mary for someone who is suffering.

02-18: The young shepherd girl of Lourdes to whom Mary appeared in 1858.

02-18.qui: Bernadette Soubirous (1844-1879), daughter of a ruined miller in Lourdes, was a poor child with little schooling.
02-18.sens: In 1858 she saw the Virgin Mary at the grotto of Massabielle. Later a nun at Nevers, where her body rests, she used to say: “My job is to tell you, not to make you believe.” In France she is celebrated on 18 February.
02-18.vivre: Simply tell the truth, without trying to convince.

02-19: A priest of Rome, martyred at the end of the third century.

02-19.qui: According to tradition, Gabinus was a priest of Rome, brother of Pope Saint Caius and father of Saint Susanna.
02-19.sens: He is said to have died in prison for his faith under the Emperor Diocletian. He is buried in the church of Saint Susanna in Rome.
02-19.vivre: Pray for a family that passes on the faith.

02-20: Saint Clare of Assisi's niece, who left a worldly life to join her.

02-20.qui: Amata (died 1252) belonged to the noble Offreduccio family of Assisi, like Saint Clare, her aunt.
02-20.sens: A very worldly young woman, she was converted while visiting her aunt at the convent of San Damiano, and entered it in 1213. She lived there in prayer until her death.
02-20.vivre: Visit someone whose faith inspires you.

02-21: Saint Peter Damian: a reforming monk who called the Church back to simplicity.

02-21.qui: Peter Damian (1007-1072), an orphan who looked after pigs as a child, became a monk and then a cardinal.
02-21.sens: He called the Church to reform and to live simply. A Doctor of the Church, he wrote beautiful texts on prayer.
02-21.vivre: Simplify one thing in your life.

02-22: We celebrate the mission given to Peter: to strengthen his brothers.

02-22.qui: On this day the Church celebrates the “chair” of Saint Peter, that is, his mission to teach and to guide.
02-22.sens: The chair is the bishop's seat. Jesus asked Peter to strengthen his brothers in faith (Lk 22:32). In Rome, in Saint Peter's Basilica, a great sculpture by Bernini encloses an ancient wooden chair.
02-22.vivre: Pray for the Pope and for those who guide the Church.

02-23: A bishop of Smyrna who had known the apostle John, martyred at 86.

02-23.qui: Polycarp (c. 69-155) was bishop of Smyrna, in Turkey.
02-23.sens: He had known the apostle John. At 86, ordered to deny Christ, he replied: “Eighty-six years I have served him, and he has done me no wrong: how can I blaspheme my King?” He died at the stake.
02-23.vivre: Give thanks for an older person whose faith inspires you.

02-24: A fifth-century bishop of Trier, in a time of invasions.

02-24.qui: Modestus was bishop of Trier, in the Rhineland, around 480.
02-24.sens: It was a very hard time: the Franks were invading the region, before the baptism of Clovis. He kept the faith alive amid the turmoil. His relics are venerated in the church of Saint Matthias in Trier.

02-25: A bishop of Pamphylia, in today's Turkey, crucified in 251.

02-25.qui: Nestor was bishop of Magydos, in Pamphylia, in the third century.
02-25.sens: During the persecution of the Emperor Decius, he advised his people to flee and let himself be arrested alone. Condemned for preferring “a crucified man” to the emperors, he was crucified in his turn.

02-26: Saint Alexander of Alexandria: the Egyptian bishop who defended the divinity of Christ at the Council of Nicaea.

02-26.qui: Alexander was bishop of Alexandria from 313 to 326.
02-26.sens: When his priest Arius taught that Christ was not truly God, he called a council and then defended the faith at the Council of Nicaea in 325, with his deacon Athanasius. He was known for his mercy towards those who had denied the faith and came back.
02-26.vivre: Say the Creed, thinking of those who defended it.

02-27: Saint Gregory of Narek: an Armenian monk and poet, Doctor of the Church, author of a great book of prayers.

02-27.qui: Gregory of Narek (c. 951-1003) was an Armenian monk.
02-27.sens: His Book of Lamentations, a long poetic prayer, is one of the treasures of Armenian literature. Pope Francis proclaimed him a Doctor of the Church in 2015.
02-27.vivre: Tell God, in your own words, what weighs on your heart.

02-28: Saint Romanus of the Jura: a hermit who went into the forests of the Jura, where other monks joined him.

02-28.qui: Romanus (c. 390-463) went to live as a hermit in the forests of the Jura.
02-28.sens: Others joined him, including his brother Lupicinus: they founded the abbey of Condat, around which the town of Saint-Claude grew up.
02-28.vivre: Take a quiet moment out in nature.

02-29: Saint Oswald of Worcester: an English bishop who washed the feet of twelve poor people every day.

02-29.qui: Oswald (died 992) was bishop of Worcester and archbishop of York, in England.
02-29.sens: He founded monasteries and served the poor himself: every day he washed the feet of twelve of them. He died while doing so.
02-29.vivre: Do a humble act of service today.

03-01: A sixth-century bishop of Angers who ransomed prisoners.

03-01.qui: Albinus (c. 470-550) was a Breton monk who became bishop of Angers.
03-01.sens: He is known for his kindness to prisoners: he paid to free those held captive. Many churches and villages in western France bear his name.
03-01.vivre: Help someone get out of a difficult situation.

03-02: Blessed Charles the Good: a count of Flanders who fed his people during a famine.

03-02.qui: Charles the Good (c. 1083-1127) was Count of Flanders, son of the Danish king Saint Canute.
03-02.sens: During a famine he had the grain in his barns handed out and forbade speculation on prices. He was murdered in a church in Bruges while praying. He has been declared blessed.
03-02.vivre: Don't take advantage of a situation at others' expense.

03-03: A Breton monk, founder of the abbey of Landévennec.

03-03.qui: Winwaloe (Guénolé, c. 460-532) was a Breton monk.
03-03.sens: He founded the abbey of Landévennec, on the roadstead of Brest, one of the oldest in Brittany. Benedictine monks still live there.
03-03.vivre: Visit, in person or in thought, a place where people have prayed for centuries.

03-04: A young prince of Poland, known for his love of the poor.

03-04.qui: Casimir (1458-1484) was a prince of Poland, the king's son.
03-04.sens: He refused to fight a war he thought unjust and preferred a life of prayer and service of the poor. He died at 25. He is the patron saint of Lithuania.
03-04.vivre: Walk away from a pointless argument.

03-05: A martyr of Brescia, in Italy, in the early centuries.

03-05.qui: Olive was a young Christian martyred in Brescia, in Lombardy.
03-05.sens: Little is known about her; her relics are venerated in Brescia. Her name recalls the olive tree, the tree of peace.

03-06: A young woman from Corbie who renewed the order of Saint Clare.

03-06.qui: Colette (1381-1447), a carpenter's daughter from Corbie in Picardy, first lived as a recluse.
03-06.sens: Then she travelled on foot across France and Flanders to renew the order of Saint Clare, founding seventeen monasteries. The Colettine Poor Clares still live by her reform.
03-06.vivre: Go back to a good habit you'd let slip.

03-07: A young mother and her servant, martyred together in Carthage in 203.

03-07.qui: Perpetua, a 22-year-old young mother, and Felicity, her pregnant slave, were arrested in Carthage in 203.
03-07.sens: Perpetua kept a diary in prison, one of the oldest writings by a Christian woman. The two young women died together in the arena, holding hands. Their names are mentioned in the Eucharistic Prayer at Mass.
03-07.vivre: Think of a friendship that makes you braver.

03-08: Saint John of God: a Portuguese man in Granada who founded a hospital for those nobody wanted.

03-08.qui: John of God (1495-1550), from Portugal, had been a shepherd, a soldier and a bookseller.
03-08.sens: In Granada, deeply moved by a sermon of Saint John of Avila, he began caring for the sick and the mentally ill whom nobody wanted, and founded a hospital. His brothers, the Brothers Hospitallers of Saint John of God, care for the sick all over the world today.
03-08.vivre: Take care of someone others avoid.

03-09: Saint Frances of Rome: a Roman wife and mother who served the sick during the plague.

03-09.qui: Frances of Rome (1384-1440), married at 13 to a Roman nobleman, was a mother.
03-09.sens: During epidemics and wars she nursed the sick and gave away her possessions. She founded a community of women serving the poor. People said she could see her guardian angel; she is the patron saint of motorists.
03-09.vivre: Thank your guardian angel before setting off on the road.

03-10: One of the Forty Martyrs of Sebaste, who froze to death on an icy lake.

03-10.qui: Vivian was one of forty Christian soldiers of a Roman legion stationed in Armenia in 320.
03-10.sens: Condemned to freeze to death, naked on a frozen lake, they supported each other in prayer; a warm bath awaited anyone who renounced the faith. According to the account, one gave in, and a guard, moved by their courage, took his place.
03-10.vivre: Support those going through the same trial as you.

03-11: A martyr of the early centuries, venerated in Swabia.

03-11.qui: Rosina was a virgin martyr of the early centuries.
03-11.sens: Almost nothing is known of her life. She has been venerated since the fourteenth century in Swabia, in southern Germany, where a chapel is dedicated to her.
03-11.vivre: Pray for the Christians no one remembers.

03-12: A Benedictine nun in Tuscany who ended her life as a recluse.

03-12.qui: Justina Bezzoli Francucci (c. 1257-1319) was a Benedictine nun of Arezzo, in Tuscany.
03-12.sens: Faithful to the Rule of Saint Benedict, she spent the last years of her life as a recluse, in prayer. She is often invoked as Saint Justina.

03-13: A priest of Córdoba, martyred in 857. On 13 March 2013, Pope Francis was elected.

03-13.qui: Roderick was a priest of Córdoba, martyred in 857 with his friend Solomon.
03-13.sens: Like Saint Eulogius, he is one of the martyrs of Córdoba. On 13 March we also remember the election of Pope Francis in 2013, the first pope from the Americas.
03-13.vivre: Pray for the Pope and for the Church.

03-14: A queen of Germany so generous she emptied the treasury for the poor.

03-14.qui: Matilda (c. 895-968) was Queen of Germany, wife of King Henry the Fowler.
03-14.sens: Very generous, she founded monasteries and hospitals. As a widow she suffered from her sons' ingratitude, and forgave them.

03-15: Saint Louise de Marillac: with Saint Vincent de Paul, she founded the Daughters of Charity.

03-15.qui: Louise de Marillac (1591-1660), a widow with one son, met Saint Vincent de Paul.
03-15.sens: With him she founded the Daughters of Charity in 1633, who went to care for the poor in their homes and in hospitals, without being enclosed in a convent: a revolution at the time. They are present all over the world today.
03-15.vivre: Visit someone who is ill or elderly.

03-16: The Poor Clare who succeeded Saint Clare at San Damiano.

03-16.qui: Benedicta (died 1260) joined Saint Clare at the convent of San Damiano in Assisi.
03-16.sens: After Clare's death in 1253, she succeeded her as abbess and faithfully kept the poverty the foundress had wanted.

03-17: Kidnapped by pirates and enslaved in Ireland, he went back to bring it the Gospel.

03-17.qui: Patrick (c. 385-461), born in Britain, was kidnapped by pirates at 16 and became a slave in Ireland.
03-17.sens: He escaped, became a priest, then returned to Ireland to preach the Gospel. Legend says he explained the Trinity with a shamrock. Saint Patrick's Day is Ireland's national day, celebrated all over the world.
03-17.vivre: Forgive someone who hurt you long ago.

03-18: Saint Cyril of Jerusalem: a bishop who explained the faith to new Christians with great clarity.

03-18.sens: His Catecheses, given to adults preparing for baptism, explain the faith and the sacraments with great clarity. He is a Doctor of the Church.
03-18.vivre: Explain something about your faith simply to a child.

03-19: Saint Joseph, Spouse of the Blessed Virgin Mary, who watched over Jesus in silence.

03-19.qui: Joseph is the husband of Mary and the foster father of Jesus.
03-19.sens: A carpenter of Nazareth, he protected his family and took them to Egypt to escape Herod; the Gospel records not a single word he spoke. He is patron of the universal Church, of fathers, of workers and of a happy death.
03-19.vivre: Do a quiet service for your family.

03-20: An English hermit, a close friend of Saint Cuthbert.

03-20.qui: Herbert (died 687) lived as a hermit on an island in Derwentwater, in England.
03-20.sens: Every year he visited his friend Saint Cuthbert to talk about God. According to Bede, he asked to die on the same day, and the two friends died on 20 March 687.
03-20.vivre: Give thanks for a friendship that brings you closer to God.

03-21: A German widow who gave her wealth to the poor and became a nun.

03-21.qui: Clementia of Hohenberg (died 1176) was the wife of the Count of Spanheim, in the Rhineland.
03-21.sens: As a widow she gave her possessions to the poor and entered a Benedictine monastery in Trier as a simple nun, where she died.
03-21.vivre: Share what you have with someone in need.

03-22: A Roman widow who chose a life of prayer and service.

03-22.qui: Lea was a noble widow of Rome in the fourth century.
03-22.sens: Saint Jerome tells how, after her husband's death, she chose a simple life of prayer and service, and led a community of women.
03-22.vivre: Change a habit so as to live more simply.

03-23: Saint Turibius of Mogrovejo: an archbishop of Lima who travelled his vast diocese on foot.

03-23.qui: Turibius of Mogrovejo (1538-1606), a Spanish lawyer, was appointed archbishop of Lima, in Peru, before he was even a priest.
03-23.sens: He crossed his huge diocese on foot, learned the local languages, defended the Indigenous peoples against abuse and confirmed Saint Rose of Lima.
03-23.vivre: Learn a few words of the language of someone you spend time with.

03-24: Saint Catherine of Sweden: Saint Bridget's daughter, who nursed her sick husband and led her mother's monastery.

03-24.qui: Catherine (c. 1331-1381) was the daughter of Saint Bridget of Sweden.
03-24.sens: Married to a young disabled nobleman whom she nursed devotedly, she joined her mother in Rome, where she learned of her husband's death. She later took Bridget's body back to Sweden and became abbess of Vadstena. 24 March is also the day Saint Óscar Romero died, in 1980.
03-24.vivre: Take care of a relative who is ill.

03-25: The angel Gabriel comes to Mary, and she says yes.

03-25.qui: The angel Gabriel is sent to Mary in Nazareth to announce that she will be the mother of the Son of God (Lk 1:26-38).
03-25.sens: Mary answers: “Here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word.” The feast falls nine months before Christmas. It is in memory of this yes that we pray the Angelus.

03-26: A Greek martyr, burned with other Christians in their church in Crimea.

03-26.qui: Larissa was one of a group of twenty-six Gothic Christians martyred around 375.
03-26.sens: A Gothic king who was still pagan had the church where they were praying set on fire. She is honoured by Greek and Russian Christians.
03-26.vivre: Pray for Christians killed in their churches.

03-27: Saint Rupert of Salzburg: the bishop who founded the city and abbey of Salzburg.

03-27.qui: Rupert (c. 660-718) was a bishop from Worms.
03-27.sens: He settled on the ruins of a Roman town and founded Saint Peter's Abbey there: the origin of Salzburg in Austria, of which he is patron. He developed salt mining there, which gave the city its name.
03-27.vivre: Take an interest in the history of your town.

03-28: A king of Burgundy who changed his ways and cared for his people in the plague.

03-28.qui: Guntram (c. 532-592) was King of Burgundy, a grandson of Clovis.
03-28.sens: At first violent like many kings of his time, he changed his life, ruled justly and cared for his people during an epidemic.

03-29: A Welsh queen who became a hermit, mother of Saint Cadoc.

03-29.qui: Gwladys was queen of a small kingdom in Wales in the fifth century.
03-29.sens: According to tradition, after a turbulent life she changed her ways together with her husband; as a widow she lived as a hermit. She was the mother of Saint Cadoc. Her story says that God forgives and lifts us up.

03-30: A sick Duke of Savoy, very kind to the poor.

03-30.qui: Amadeus (1435-1472), born in Thonon, was Duke of Savoy, married to Yolande of France; they had seven children.
03-30.sens: Suffering from epilepsy, he lived his illness with faith and let his wife govern. He is remembered for his great charity towards the poor.

03-31: A deacon of Persia, martyred in the fifth century for refusing to keep quiet.

03-31.qui: Benjamin was a deacon in Persia in the fifth century.
03-31.sens: Imprisoned for his faith, he was released on condition that he stop speaking about Christ; he refused to keep quiet and died a martyr.
03-31.vivre: Don't hide your faith when someone asks you about it.

04-01: Saint Hugh of Grenoble: the bishop who welcomed Saint Bruno and helped him found the Grande Chartreuse.

04-01.qui: Hugh (1053-1132) was bishop of Grenoble for more than fifty years.
04-01.sens: In 1084 he welcomed Saint Bruno and his companions and gave them the wilderness of Chartreuse, where they founded the Grande Chartreuse.
04-01.vivre: Offer your help to a project that is just starting.

04-02: Saint Francis of Paola: a hermit from Calabria who founded the Minims, the “least ones”.

04-02.qui: Francis of Paola (1416-1507) was a hermit from Calabria, in Italy.
04-02.sens: He founded the Order of Minims, the “least ones”, who live in great humility. King Louis XI of France summoned him to his deathbed; Francis stayed on in France, at Plessis-lès-Tours. 2 April is also the anniversary of the death of John Paul II, in 2005.
04-02.vivre: Choose the last place at least once today.

04-03: Saint Richard of Chichester: an English bishop who wrote a famous prayer to know Christ better.

04-03.qui: Richard of Wyche (1197-1253) was bishop of Chichester, in England.
04-03.sens: He lived very simply and defended the poor. A prayer is attributed to him asking to know Jesus more clearly, love him more dearly and follow him more nearly, day by day.
04-03.vivre: Ask Jesus to help you know him better.

04-04: Saint Isidore of Seville: a learned bishop who set out to gather all the knowledge of his time.

04-04.sens: A great scholar, he wrote the Etymologies, an encyclopedia of all the knowledge of his day that was read throughout the Middle Ages. He is a Doctor of the Church and has been suggested as patron saint of the Internet.

04-05: A young martyr of Thessalonica who hid the holy books.

04-05.qui: Irene was a young Christian of Thessalonica, martyred in 304 with her sisters Agape and Chionia.
04-05.sens: During Diocletian's persecution she hid the books of the Bible despite the ban. Arrested, she refused to deny her faith and was burned. Her name means “peace” in Greek.
04-05.vivre: Take care of your Bible and read it.

04-06: A pope who sent missionaries to Ireland and defended Mary as Mother of God.

04-06.sens: He supported Saint Cyril of Alexandria at the Council of Ephesus in 431, which proclaimed Mary “Mother of God”. He also sent Palladius to bring the Gospel to Ireland.
04-06.vivre: Pray for the unity of the Church.

04-07: Saint John Baptist de La Salle: a priest of Reims who founded free schools for poor children.

04-07.qui: John Baptist de La Salle (1651-1719), a canon of Reims, came from a wealthy family.
04-07.sens: He gave away his fortune to found the Brothers of the Christian Schools, who opened free schools for poor children. He invented new methods: teaching in French rather than Latin, teaching pupils in groups. He is the patron saint of teachers.
04-07.vivre: Thank a teacher who helped you.

04-08: Saint Julie Billiart: paralysed for twenty years, she founded a congregation to educate girls.

04-08.qui: Julie Billiart (1751-1816), the daughter of farmers in Picardy, was paralysed for more than twenty years.
04-08.sens: In Amiens she founded the Sisters of Notre Dame to teach poor girls, and regained the use of her legs. Her motto: “How good the good God is!”

04-09: Saint Maximus of Alexandria: a third-century bishop of Alexandria who shared his bishop's exile.

04-09.qui: Maximus was a priest, then bishop of Alexandria from 264 to 282.
04-09.sens: He shared the exile of his bishop, Saint Dionysius, during the persecution, and then succeeded him. He supported the theological school of Alexandria.
04-09.vivre: Stay loyal to a friend in hard times.

04-10: Saint Fulbert of Chartres: the bishop who rebuilt Chartres Cathedral after a fire.

04-10.qui: Fulbert (c. 960-1028) was bishop of Chartres and a great scholar.
04-10.sens: After the fire of 1020 he had Chartres Cathedral rebuilt. He ran a famous school and composed hymns.
04-10.vivre: Take time to look at a stained-glass window or a beautiful church.

04-11: A bishop of Kraków, martyred in 1079, patron saint of Poland.

04-11.sens: He rebuked King Bolesław for his cruelty; the king killed him during Mass. He is the patron saint of Poland.
04-11.vivre: Tell the truth with courage and gentleness.

04-12: A pope who defended faith in the Trinity.

04-12.sens: He welcomed the exiled Saint Athanasius to Rome and defended the faith of the Council of Nicaea: Jesus is truly God. He had several basilicas built in Rome.
04-12.vivre: Make the sign of the cross thinking of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.

04-13: Saint Ida of Boulogne: a countess, mother of Godfrey of Bouillon and friend of Saint Anselm.

04-13.qui: Ida (c. 1040-1113), daughter of the Duke of Lower Lorraine, married Count Eustace of Boulogne.
04-13.sens: Very devout, she exchanged spiritual letters with Saint Anselm, founded monasteries and helped the poor. She was the mother of Godfrey of Bouillon.
04-13.vivre: Write a letter to someone who guides you.

04-14: Saint Maximus, martyr of Rome, converted by the courage of other Christians.

04-14.qui: Maximus was martyred in Rome in the third century, with Tiburtius and Valerian.
04-14.sens: According to tradition he was an official who was converted by the faith of Valerian, Saint Cecilia's husband, and his brother Tiburtius, and died with them.
04-14.vivre: Let your faith show in what you do.

04-15: The first bishop of Vannes, in Brittany.

04-15.qui: Paternus was bishop of Vannes in the fifth century.
04-15.sens: Little is known about him; old accounts make him a monk who travelled between Brittany and Wales. He is one of the seven founding saints of Brittany.

04-16: Saint Benedict Joseph Labre: a poor pilgrim who lived on the streets of Rome, praying in its churches.

04-16.qui: Benedict Joseph Labre (1748-1783), born in Artois, tried several monasteries but was not accepted.
04-16.sens: He became a pilgrim and walked across Europe, then lived poor on the streets of Rome, spending his days praying in churches. People called him “the poor man of the Forty Hours”. It is also the day Saint Bernadette died, in 1879.
04-16.vivre: Look respectfully at someone who lives on the street.

04-17: Saint Kateri Tekakwitha: a young Iroquois woman who became Christian, the first Native American saint.

04-17.qui: Kateri Tekakwitha (1656-1680) was a young Iroquois woman, daughter of a Mohawk chief and a Christian Algonquin mother.
04-17.sens: Scarred by smallpox, she discovered the faith, was baptized and lived near Montreal. She was the first Native American saint, canonized in 2012.

04-18: Saint Perfectus of Córdoba: a priest of Córdoba, martyred in 850.

04-18.qui: Perfectus was a priest of Córdoba, martyred in 850.
04-18.sens: Questioned about his faith by Muslims, he answered frankly and was executed. He was the first of the ninth-century martyrs of Córdoba.
04-18.vivre: Pray for dialogue between Christians and Muslims.

04-19: A martyr of Carthage who asked that his mother and sister be spared.

04-19.qui: Mappalicus was a Christian of Carthage, martyred in 250.
04-19.sens: During the persecution of Decius he asked that his mother and sister, who had wavered, be left in peace, and himself died under torture. Saint Cyprian praised him.

04-20: A young woman of Brabant who said no to a forced marriage.

04-20.qui: Oda (died 1158) was born into a noble family in Brabant, in Belgium.
04-20.sens: On the day her parents wanted to marry her against her will, she said “no” at the altar. She became a Premonstratensian nun.
04-20.vivre: Pray for those forced to do what they don't want.

04-21: A monk from Aosta who became Archbishop of Canterbury: “faith seeking understanding”.

04-21.qui: Anselm (1033-1109), born in Aosta, was a monk at Le Bec in Normandy, then Archbishop of Canterbury.
04-21.sens: He is one of the great thinkers of the Middle Ages; his motto: “faith seeking understanding”. He defended the Church's freedom against the King of England. He is a Doctor of the Church.
04-21.vivre: Take time to think about your faith.

04-22: A young Christian of Lyon, martyred with his friend Alexander.

04-22.qui: Epipodius was a young man from Lyon, martyred around 178.
04-22.sens: With his friend Alexander he escaped the persecution of 177 at first, but was later arrested. They died for their faith, Epipodius beheaded and Alexander crucified.
04-22.vivre: Give thanks for a faithful friend.

04-23: The dragon saint. In Catalonia he is Sant Jordi: people give a rose and a book.

04-23.qui: George was a soldier martyred in Palestine around 303.
04-23.sens: A medieval legend tells how he killed a dragon to rescue a princess: he stands for the victory of good over evil. He is patron saint of England and of Catalonia: in Barcelona, on Sant Jordi, people give a rose and a book.
04-23.vivre: Give someone a book you have loved.

04-24: Saint Fidelis of Sigmaringen: a lawyer for the poor who became a Capuchin and was martyred in Switzerland.

04-24.qui: Fidelis of Sigmaringen (1578-1622) was a lawyer who defended the poor for free.
04-24.sens: As a Capuchin, he preached in Switzerland at a time of religious conflict and was killed there. He is the patron saint of lawyers.
04-24.vivre: Do someone a favour for free.

04-25: The author of the shortest of the four Gospels.

04-25.qui: Mark is the author of the shortest of the four Gospels, probably the oldest.
04-25.sens: A companion of Peter and Paul, he is thought to have written down Peter's teaching in Rome. His symbol is the lion. He is the patron saint of Venice, where his relics were taken.
04-25.vivre: Read a chapter of Mark's Gospel.

04-26: A widow of Siena who nursed the sick in hospital.

04-26.qui: Alda, or Aldobrandesca (c. 1249-1309), was a noblewoman of Siena.
04-26.sens: Widowed at thirty, she joined a Third Order and spent the rest of her life caring for the sick in her city's hospital.
04-26.vivre: Ask after someone who is ill.

04-27: A servant of Lucca, in Italy, patron saint of domestic workers.

04-27.qui: Zita (c. 1218-1278) was a servant in Lucca, in Italy.
04-27.sens: She worked all her life for the same family, with patience and kindness, and gave what she could to the poor. She is the patron saint of domestic workers. In Catalonia, 27 April is also the feast of Our Lady of Montserrat.
04-27.vivre: Thank the people who serve you day to day.

04-28: Saint Peter Chanel: the first martyr of Oceania, missionary on Futuna.

04-28.qui: Peter Chanel (1803-1841), a priest from the Ain region of France, joined the Marists to go on mission.
04-28.sens: He landed on the island of Futuna in the Pacific in 1837. He was killed in 1841, but soon afterwards the whole island became Christian. He is the patron saint of Oceania.
04-28.vivre: Pray for the Christians of Oceania.

04-29: Saint Catherine of Siena: a young laywoman who dared to write to the Pope asking him to return to Rome.

04-29.qui: Catherine of Siena (1347-1380) was a young Dominican laywoman, the twenty-fourth child of a dyer.
04-29.sens: She nursed the sick, reconciled feuding families and wrote to the Pope, then living in Avignon, to persuade him to return to Rome, which he did. She is a Doctor of the Church and patron saint of Europe and of Italy.
04-29.vivre: Dare to say respectfully what you believe is right.

04-30: A Lombard shepherd boy who became pope and stayed simple and poor.

04-30.qui: Antonio Ghislieri (1504-1572), a shepherd boy, joined the Dominicans and became pope in 1566.
04-30.sens: He carried out the reforms of the Council of Trent, published the Roman Missal and Catechism, and lived austerely. After the victory of Lepanto in 1571, he instituted a feast of thanksgiving that became Our Lady of the Rosary.
04-30.vivre: Pray a decade of the rosary.

05-01: Saint Joseph the Worker, on Labour Day: the craftsman of Nazareth.

05-01.qui: Joseph, Mary's husband, was a carpenter in Nazareth; Jesus learned the trade from him.
05-01.sens: In 1955 Pope Pius XII placed 1 May, Labour Day in many countries, under the protection of Saint Joseph the Worker, to say that human work has value in God's eyes.

05-02: A bishop of Alexandria, exiled five times for defending the divinity of Christ.

05-02.qui: Athanasius (c. 296-373) was bishop of Alexandria, in Egypt.
05-02.sens: All his life he defended the faith of the Council of Nicaea: Jesus is truly God. For this he was exiled five times. He also wrote the Life of Saint Anthony, which made the desert monks known.
05-02.vivre: Hold firm to a just conviction, without aggression.

05-03.qui: Philip and James the Less are two of the twelve apostles.
05-03.sens: Philip is the one who said to Jesus: “Show us the Father” (Jn 14:8). James, called “the brother of the Lord”, led the Church in Jerusalem. Their relics rest together in Rome, in the church of the Holy Apostles.
05-03.vivre: Ask Jesus to show you the Father.

05-04: Saint Silvanus of Gaza: a bishop of Gaza, sentenced to the mines and martyred with thirty-nine companions.

05-04.qui: Silvanus was a priest and then bishop of Gaza, in Palestine, in the early fourth century.
05-04.sens: A gentle, peaceable man, he was sentenced to the copper mines with other Christians, mutilated, then beheaded in 311.
05-04.vivre: Pray for peace in Gaza and the Holy Land.

05-05: A widow from Thuringia who founded a hospital in Prussia.

05-05.qui: Jutta of Sangerhausen (died 1260) was a noblewoman of Thuringia, widowed very young.
05-05.sens: She left her homeland for Prussia, where she nursed the sick and lived poorly near Kulmsee. She is the patron saint of Prussia. Her name, Judith, is also that of a Bible heroine who saved her people through her courage.
05-05.vivre: Take care of someone who is ill or alone.

05-06: Saint James Chastan: a priest from Provence, missionary and martyr in Korea.

05-06.qui: Jacques-Honoré Chastan (1803-1839), born in the Alps of Haute-Provence, was a priest of the Paris Foreign Missions.
05-06.sens: He entered Korea secretly, where the faith was forbidden, and was beheaded there in 1839. He was canonized in 1984 with one hundred and two other Korean martyrs.
05-06.vivre: Pray for the Christians of Korea.

05-07: A queen of Hungary, wife of Saint Stephen.

05-07.qui: Gisela (c. 985-1060), a Bavarian princess, married King Stephen of Hungary.
05-07.sens: She worked with him to bring the Gospel to the country. Widowed and driven from the kingdom, she became an abbess in Bavaria. She was declared blessed in 1975.
05-07.vivre: Support your spouse or someone close to you in their mission.

05-08: Saint Desideratus of Bourges: a sixth-century bishop of Bourges, formerly the king's chancellor.

05-08.qui: Desideratus (died 550) was chancellor to the King of the Franks, then bishop of Bourges.
05-08.sens: At a court full of violence, he stayed upright and sought peace. As bishop he helped make Gaul Christian. 8 May is also the anniversary of the end of the war in Europe in 1945 and, in 2025, the day Pope Leo XIV was elected.
05-08.vivre: Pray for peace in the world.

05-09: A former Egyptian soldier who founded the first monasteries where monks live in community.

05-09.qui: Pachomius (c. 292-348) was a former Egyptian soldier.
05-09.sens: Moved by the charity of Christians who fed the conscripts, he was converted. He founded the first monasteries where monks lived together under a common rule: the beginning of community monastic life.
05-09.vivre: Do something helpful for your family or community.

05-10: A young shepherdess of Berry, martyred in the ninth century, patron saint of Berry.

05-10.qui: Solange was a young shepherdess in Berry, in France, in the ninth century.
05-10.sens: According to tradition, she rejected a lord's advances and died a martyr. She is the patron saint of Berry; a village near Bourges bears her name.
05-10.vivre: Pray for young people under pressure.

05-11: A martyr of Saintes who became patron of the Provençal poets of the Félibrige.

05-11.qui: According to tradition, Estelle was a martyr of Saintes, in Saintonge.
05-11.sens: Her name means “star”. In the nineteenth century the poet Frédéric Mistral and his friends, who wanted to revive the Provençal language, chose her as patron of their movement, the Félibrige, and took the star as its emblem.
05-11.vivre: Read a poem in your mother tongue.

05-12: Saint Achillius of Larissa: a Greek bishop at the Council of Nicaea, attentive to the poor.

05-12.qui: Achillius was bishop of Larissa, in Thessaly, in the fourth century.
05-12.sens: A pilgrim to Jerusalem and Rome, he was a shepherd attentive to the poor, the sick and strangers. He took part in the Council of Nicaea in 325.

05-13: On 13 May 1917, Mary appeared to three children in Portugal.

05-13.qui: On 13 May 1917, at Fatima in Portugal, three shepherd children, Lucia, Francisco and Jacinta, saw the Virgin Mary.
05-13.sens: She appeared to them six times, until 13 October, and asked them to pray the rosary for peace. On 13 May 1981, the anniversary, John Paul II was shot in Saint Peter's Square; he credited Our Lady of Fatima with his survival.
05-13.vivre: Pray a decade of the rosary for peace.

05-14: The apostle chosen to replace Judas.

05-14.qui: Matthias is the apostle chosen to replace Judas.
05-14.sens: After the Ascension, the apostles prayed and then cast lots between two disciples who had followed Jesus from the beginning: the lot fell to Matthias (Acts 1:15-26).
05-14.vivre: Accept with trust a place you hadn't expected.

05-15: A young martyr of Lampsacus, in Turkey, in the third century.

05-15.qui: Dionysia was a young Christian martyred around 250 at Lampsacus, on the Dardanelles.
05-15.sens: According to the account, she threw herself into the arena to die with three condemned companions, Peter, Andrew and Paul, rather than deny her faith. 15 May is also the feast of Saint Isidore the Farmer, patron saint of Madrid.
05-15.vivre: Stand by those who are suffering.

05-16: A bishop of Amiens, patron saint of bakers.

05-16.qui: Honoratus was bishop of Amiens in the sixth century.
05-16.sens: It is said that the baker's peel used to announce his election sprouted leaves: he became the patron saint of bakers. The Rue du Faubourg-Saint-Honoré in Paris is named after him.
05-16.vivre: Thank your baker for their work.

05-17: Saint Paschal Baylon: an Aragonese shepherd who became a friar porter, in love with the Eucharist.

05-17.qui: Paschal Baylon (1540-1592) was a shepherd from Aragon who became a Franciscan brother.
05-17.sens: As doorkeeper of his friary, he welcomed everyone with joy and spent long hours in adoration before the Blessed Sacrament. He is the patron of Eucharistic Congresses.
05-17.vivre: Spend a few minutes in a church, before the tabernacle.

05-18: A twelfth-century King of Sweden, patron of his country.

05-18.sens: He ruled his kingdom justly and supported the evangelization of Finland with Saint Henry. He was killed as he left Mass. He is the patron saint of Sweden; Uppsala Cathedral keeps his relics.
05-18.vivre: Do your duty fairly and honestly.

05-19: A Breton judge, the advocate of the poor, patron saint of lawyers.

05-19.qui: Ivo Hélory (1253-1303) was a Breton priest and judge in Tréguier.
05-19.sens: He defended the poor in court for free and refused gifts. People called him “the advocate of the poor”. He is patron saint of lawyers and of Brittany; the “pardon of Saint Ivo” draws thousands to Tréguier every year.
05-19.vivre: Stand up for someone who is unfairly accused.

05-20: Saint Bernardine of Siena: a preacher who held up the name of Jesus to the crowds.

05-20.qui: Bernardine of Siena (1380-1444) was an Italian Franciscan and a great preacher.
05-20.sens: He would show the crowds a tablet bearing the letters IHS, the monogram of the name of Jesus, and invite them to pray that name. He is the patron saint of advertisers and communicators.
05-20.vivre: Pray by gently repeating the name of Jesus.

05-21: The Roman emperor who ended the persecution of Christians.

05-21.qui: Constantine (c. 272-337), son of Saint Helena, became emperor.
05-21.sens: In 313 the Edict of Milan granted Christians freedom of worship. He called the Council of Nicaea in 325 and was baptized shortly before his death. The Eastern Churches honour him as a saint with his mother; the Catholic Church recognizes his role without listing him among the saints of its calendar.
05-21.vivre: Give thanks for the freedom to believe.

05-22: A wife and mother of Cascia, patron saint of impossible causes.

05-22.qui: Rita (1381-1457) was a wife and mother in Cascia, in Italy.
05-22.sens: Her violent husband eventually changed, then was murdered; she forgave the killers. As a widow she became a nun. She is the patron saint of impossible causes; roses are blessed in her honour.
05-22.vivre: Entrust to God a situation that seems hopeless.

05-23: Saint Desiderius of Vienne: a bishop of Vienne, martyred in the seventh century.

05-23.qui: Desiderius was bishop of Vienne, in the Dauphiné, in the seventh century.
05-23.sens: He rebuked Queen Brunhilda for her conduct, was exiled, then murdered around 607. Several towns and villages in France bear his name.

05-24: Two brothers of Nantes, martyred around 290.

05-24.qui: Donatian and Rogatian were two brothers of Nantes at the end of the third century.
05-24.sens: Donatian, a Christian, converted his brother; Rogatian had not yet been baptized when they were arrested. They died together. They are called “the children of Nantes” and are the city's patron saints.
05-24.vivre: Pray for your brother, your sister or a close friend.

05-25: Saint Madeleine Sophie Barat: foundress of the Society of the Sacred Heart, who educated thousands of girls.

05-25.qui: Madeleine Sophie Barat (1779-1865), a cooper's daughter from Joigny, was taught by her brother, a priest.
05-25.sens: In 1800 she founded the Society of the Sacred Heart, devoted to educating girls. By her death her sisters ran more than eighty houses in Europe and America.
05-25.vivre: Encourage a child in their studies.

05-26: Saint Philip Neri: the saint of joy, who made Rome laugh while converting it.

05-26.qui: Philip Neri (1515-1595) was a Florentine priest who settled in Rome.
05-26.sens: Joyful and full of humour, he gathered young people to pray, sing and serve the poor. He founded the Oratory. He is called “the saint of joy”.
05-26.vivre: Make someone laugh who needs it.

05-27: Saint Augustine of Canterbury: a monk sent from Rome to bring the Gospel to the English.

05-27.qui: Augustine (died c. 604) was a monk of Rome.
05-27.sens: Pope Gregory the Great sent him in 597 to evangelize the Anglo-Saxons. He baptized the King of Kent and became the first Archbishop of Canterbury.

05-28: Saint Germanus of Paris: a bishop of Paris, very generous to the poor and to captives.

05-28.sens: Very generous, he ransomed captives and helped the poor. The church of Saint-Germain-des-Prés in Paris bears his name.
05-28.vivre: Give to a charity that helps the poorest.

05-29: Saint Ursula Ledóchowska: a Polish nun, missionary in Russia and Scandinavia.

05-29.qui: Ursula Ledóchowska (1865-1939), born in Austria to a Polish family, was an Ursuline in Kraków.
05-29.sens: She went on mission to Saint Petersburg, then to Scandinavia, and founded the Ursulines of the Agonizing Heart of Jesus. She was canonized in 2003.

05-30: Saint Joan of Arc: a young peasant girl from Lorraine who followed her voices to the end.

05-30.qui: Joan of Arc (1412-1431) was a young peasant girl from Domrémy, in Lorraine.
05-30.sens: At 13 she heard voices sending her to free France. She liberated Orléans and had the king crowned at Reims. Captured and tried by a biased Church court, she was burned at the stake in Rouen on 30 May 1431. Rehabilitated in 1456, she was canonized in 1920. She is one of the patron saints of France.
05-30.vivre: Stay true to what you know is right, even alone.

05-31.qui: Mary, who has just learned that she is expecting Jesus, hurries to visit her cousin Elizabeth, who is expecting John the Baptist.
05-31.sens: At her greeting, the child leaps in Elizabeth's womb, and she cries out: “Blessed are you among women.” Mary then sings the Magnificat (Lk 1:39-56). The feast closes the month of May, Mary's month.
05-31.vivre: Visit someone you haven't seen in a long time.

06-01: A philosopher who looked for the truth everywhere and found it in Christ.

06-01.qui: Justin (c. 100-165), born in Samaria, looked for truth among all the philosophers.
06-01.sens: An old man introduced him to the prophets and to Christ. As a Christian he explained the faith to pagans; he described Sunday Mass as it was already celebrated. He died a martyr in Rome.

06-02: Saint Blandina and her companions, martyred in 177 in the amphitheatre of Lyon.

06-02.qui: In 177, in Lyon, a persecution struck the city's Christians.
06-02.sens: Bishop Pothinus, aged 90, died in prison. The young slave Blandina, frail as she was, showed extraordinary courage in the amphitheatre. A letter from the time tells of their martyrdom. They are the first known martyrs of Gaul.
06-02.vivre: Pray for those who are afraid.

06-03: Saint Charles Lwanga and companions: young martyrs of Uganda, in 1886.

06-03.qui: Charles Lwanga and his companions were young Christians in Uganda.
06-03.sens: Pages at the court of King Mwanga, they refused to give in to his demands and were burned alive in 1886. They were canonized in 1964. The shrine at Namugongo draws hundreds of thousands of pilgrims every year.
06-03.vivre: Pray for young Christians in Africa.

06-04: The queen who led Clovis to baptism.

06-04.qui: Clotilde (c. 475-545) was a Christian Burgundian princess, wife of Clovis, King of the Franks.
06-04.sens: She prayed for a long time for her husband's conversion, and he was baptized by Saint Remigius at Reims. As a widow she retired to Tours, near the tomb of Saint Martin.
06-04.vivre: Pray patiently for someone close to you.

06-05: An English monk, the apostle of Germany.

06-05.qui: Boniface (c. 675-754), an English monk, is the apostle of Germany.
06-05.sens: He founded monasteries and dioceses, including Fulda. According to tradition, he had a sacred oak dedicated to a pagan god cut down. He died a martyr in Frisia with his companions.
06-05.vivre: Pray for the Church in Germany.

06-06: A nobleman converted after lightning threw him to the ground; he founded the Premonstratensians.

06-06.qui: Norbert (c. 1080-1134) was a Rhineland nobleman living a worldly life.
06-06.sens: One day, during a storm, lightning struck near him and knocked him down: he changed his life. He founded the Premonstratensian order near Laon, then became Archbishop of Magdeburg.
06-06.vivre: Change one thing in your life, starting today.

06-07: Saint Gilbert of Neuffontaines: a knight of Auvergne who became a monk and founded a hospital.

06-07.qui: Gilbert (died 1152) was a nobleman from Auvergne who went on the Second Crusade.
06-07.sens: On his return, in agreement with his wife Petronilla, he joined the Premonstratensians and founded the abbey of Neuffontaines with a hospital; his wife founded a monastery for women.
06-07.vivre: Make an important decision together as a family.

06-08: A bishop of Noyon whom French farmers link with the rain.

06-08.qui: Medard (c. 456-545) was bishop of Noyon, in Picardy.
06-08.sens: According to legend, an eagle sheltered him from the rain. A French proverb says that if it rains on Saint Medard's day, it will rain for forty more days. Farmers call on him.
06-08.vivre: Give thanks for the rain and the sun.

06-09: A Syrian deacon, “the harp of the Holy Spirit”, author of many hymns.

06-09.qui: Ephrem (c. 306-373) was a deacon in Syria, at Nisibis and then Edessa.
06-09.sens: He wrote hundreds of hymns so that ordinary people could sing the faith: he is called “the harp of the Holy Spirit”. He is a Doctor of the Church.
06-09.vivre: Sing a church hymn you love.

06-10: A bishop of Paris who founded the city's first hospital.

06-10.qui: Landericus (Landry) was bishop of Paris in the seventh century.
06-10.sens: During a famine he sold the Church's goods to feed the poor. He is credited with founding the first hospital in Paris, the Hôtel-Dieu, next to Notre-Dame.
06-10.vivre: Think of those who go hungry near where you live.

06-11: Saint Paul's companion, “a good man, full of the Holy Spirit”.

06-11.qui: Barnabas was a Jew from Cyprus, a companion of Saint Paul, and is called an apostle.
06-11.sens: Acts describes him as “a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and of faith” (Acts 11:24). It was he who introduced Paul, the former persecutor, to the apostles who did not trust him.
06-11.vivre: Trust someone others are wary of.

06-12: Blessed Guy of Cortona: a man of Cortona who welcomed Saint Francis and followed him.

06-12.qui: Guy Vignotelli (died 1245) was a modest but very hospitable man of Cortona, in Tuscany.
06-12.sens: He welcomed Saint Francis and his companions into his home, washed their feet and served them a good meal. Moved, he became a Franciscan in 1211 and lived in prayer near Cortona.
06-12.vivre: Welcome someone into your home generously.

06-13: Saint Anthony of Padua: the great-hearted preacher we pray to when we lose something.

06-13.qui: Anthony (1195-1231), born in Lisbon, became a Franciscan after seeing the bodies of the martyrs of Morocco brought home.
06-13.sens: A great preacher, he spoke so powerfully that it was said fish came to listen. He died in Padua aged 36. He is a Doctor of the Church, and people pray to him to find lost things.
06-13.vivre: Ask Saint Anthony to help you find what really matters.

06-14: Elijah's disciple, who healed Naaman and raised a child to life.

06-14.qui: Elisha was a prophet of Israel in the ninth century BC, a disciple of the prophet Elijah.
06-14.sens: When Elijah was taken up to heaven, Elisha received his cloak and his spirit. He healed Naaman, a Syrian general with leprosy, and raised the son of a woman who had welcomed him (2 Kings, chapters 2 to 5). The Martyrology remembers him on 14 June.
06-14.vivre: Welcome someone into your home generously.

06-15: Saint Germaine of Pibrac: a mistreated little shepherdess who shared her bread with those poorer than her.

06-15.qui: Germaine Cousin (c. 1579-1601) was a little shepherdess from Pibrac, near Toulouse.
06-15.sens: Sickly and mistreated by her stepmother, she lived in the stable and shared her bread with those even poorer. It is said the bread hidden in her apron turned into flowers. She died at 22.
06-15.vivre: Share your meal with someone in need.

06-16: Saint John Francis Regis: a Jesuit missionary in the mountains of the Velay and Vivarais.

06-16.qui: John Francis Regis (1597-1640) was a French Jesuit.
06-16.sens: A missionary in the mountains of the Velay and Vivarais, he crossed the countryside in winter and helped the poor and women in distress. He died at La Louvesc, in the Ardèche, where pilgrims still come.
06-16.vivre: Walk a little way to visit someone.

06-17: A blind Breton monk, guided by a wolf in legend, patron saint of Breton singers.

06-17.qui: Herve was a Breton monk of the sixth century, blind from birth.
06-17.sens: According to legend, a wolf that had eaten his donkey became his guide. A musician and singer, he is the patron saint of Breton singers and bards.
06-17.vivre: Sing a song for someone you love.

06-18: A Christian soldier of Tripoli, in Lebanon, martyred for preaching the Gospel.

06-18.qui: Leontius was a soldier stationed at Tripoli, in Lebanon, in the fourth century.
06-18.sens: He spoke about Christ to those around him and was martyred for it. His cult is very popular in the Eastern Churches.
06-18.vivre: Pray for the Christians of Lebanon.

06-19: A monk who founded the Camaldolese, between community life and life as a hermit.

06-19.qui: Romuald (c. 951-1027), a nobleman of Ravenna, entered a monastery after seeing his father kill a man in a duel.
06-19.sens: He founded the Camaldolese order, which combines life in community with the life of a hermit.
06-19.vivre: Find a balance between others and solitude.

06-20: An exiled pope who chose to step down to restore peace.

06-20.sens: He refused to reinstate a heretical patriarch of Constantinople; the Empress Theodora had him exiled to an island. He abdicated to avoid a schism and died soon after.
06-20.vivre: Choose peace rather than being right.

06-21: Saint Aloysius Gonzaga: a young Jesuit who died at 23 nursing plague victims.

06-21.qui: Aloysius Gonzaga (1568-1591), son of an Italian prince, gave up his inheritance to become a Jesuit.
06-21.sens: During a plague epidemic in Rome he nursed the sick and died at 23. He is the patron saint of young people. 21 June is also often the first day of summer.
06-21.vivre: Pray for a young person looking for their way.

06-22: Saint Thomas More: a Lord Chancellor of England, husband and father, who died for his conscience.

06-22.qui: Thomas More (1478-1535), a lawyer, writer and family man, was Lord Chancellor of England.
06-22.sens: He refused to recognize King Henry VIII as head of the Church of England, and was beheaded. Before he died he said he was “the king's good servant, but God's first”. The Church celebrates on the same day Bishop John Fisher, who died for the same reason.
06-22.vivre: Stay true to your conscience, with humour and peace.

06-23: An English queen who became abbess and founder of Ely.

06-23.qui: Etheldreda, or Audrey (c. 636-679), was a princess of East Anglia married twice for political reasons.
06-23.sens: She founded the abbey of Ely in England and became its abbess. She was one of the most popular saints of medieval England.
06-23.vivre: Pray for people who are not free to choose their path in life.

06-24: The Nativity of Saint John the Baptist
The birth of the one who prepares the way for Jesus. It is Midsummer.

06-24.qui: John the Baptist is the son of Zechariah and Elizabeth, the cousin of Jesus.
06-24.sens: He is the only saint besides Mary whose birth is celebrated. It falls six months before Christmas, as the days begin to shorten; John said of Jesus: “He must increase, but I must decrease” (Jn 3:30). Bonfires are lit for Saint John's Eve.
06-24.vivre: Step aside to make room for someone else.

06-25: Saint Prosper of Aquitaine: a married lay theologian, secretary to Pope Saint Leo.

06-25.qui: Prosper (c. 390-c. 455), born in Aquitaine, was a married layman and a disciple of Saint Augustine.
06-25.sens: He worked in the chancery of Pope Leo the Great and wrote about God's grace. He wrote to his wife: “Lift me up if I fall.”
06-25.vivre: Tell your spouse or a friend that you count on them.

06-26: A Carthusian who became bishop of Belley, in Savoy.

06-26.qui: Anthelm (1107-1178), born at the castle of Chignin in Savoy, became a Carthusian.
06-26.sens: As prior of the Grande Chartreuse, he rebuilt it after an avalanche. As bishop of Belley, he courageously defended the rights of the Church.
06-26.vivre: Patiently rebuild what has been damaged.

06-27: Saint Cyril of Alexandria: a bishop who defended Mary's title, Mother of God.

06-27.sens: At the Council of Ephesus in 431 he upheld that Mary can be called “Mother of God”, since Jesus is truly God. He is a Doctor of the Church.
06-27.vivre: Pray the Hail Mary: “Holy Mary, Mother of God”.

06-28: Saint Irenaeus of Lyon: a bishop of Lyon who said: “The glory of God is man fully alive.”

06-28.qui: Irenaeus (c. 130-202), who came from Smyrna, was bishop of Lyon.
06-28.sens: He wrote against false teachings and showed that the faith has been faithfully handed down from the apostles. He said: “The glory of God is man fully alive.” Pope Francis proclaimed him a Doctor of the Church in 2022, with the title “Doctor of Unity”.
06-28.vivre: Do something that makes you feel more alive.

06-29: The two pillars of the Church, who died in Rome.

06-29.qui: Peter the fisherman and Paul the former persecutor are the two great pillars of the Church.
06-29.sens: Both died as martyrs in Rome around 64-67: Peter crucified, Paul beheaded. They are celebrated together to show that the Church needs the faithfulness of one and the missionary drive of the other. On this day the Pope gives the pallium to new archbishops.
06-29.vivre: Pray for the Pope and for missionaries.

06-30.qui: Martial was bishop of Limoges in the third century.
06-30.sens: Later legends made him a disciple of Jesus; in fact, we only know that he founded the Church of Limoges. Every seven years the Limousin “ostensions”, listed by UNESCO, honour his relics.
06-30.vivre: Pray for the Christians of your town.

07-01: A sixth-century abbot of Mont-d'Or, near Reims.

07-01.qui: Theodoric (died c. 533) was a disciple of Saint Remigius.
07-01.sens: He founded a monastery at Mont-d'Or, near Reims, which drew many monks. It is said he had first converted his own father, a brigand.
07-01.vivre: Pray for a family member who has drifted away.

07-02: According to tradition, Saint Peter's jailers, baptized by him.

07-02.qui: According to tradition, Processus and Martinian were the jailers of Saints Peter and Paul in Rome.
07-02.sens: Witnessing their faith, they are said to have been converted and baptized by Peter with water from a spring that gushed up in the Mamertine Prison, before dying as martyrs.
07-02.vivre: Let your faith show in what you do.

07-03: Saint Thomas, the apostle who doubted, then said to Jesus: “My Lord and my God!”

07-03.qui: Thomas is one of the twelve apostles, also called Didymus, “the twin”.
07-03.sens: Absent when the risen Jesus appeared to the disciples, he wanted to see and touch his wounds. Eight days later he said: “My Lord and my God!” (Jn 20:28). According to tradition, he took the Gospel as far as India.
07-03.vivre: Tell God your doubts, without shame.

07-04: Saint Elizabeth of Portugal: a peacemaking queen who reconciled her husband and her son.

07-04.qui: Elizabeth (1271-1336), a princess of Aragon, became Queen of Portugal.
07-04.sens: Several times she stepped in to prevent war between her husband and her son, and between neighbouring kingdoms. She founded hospitals and shelters. She is called “the queen of peace”.
07-04.vivre: Be a peacemaker in your family.

07-05: Saint Anthony Mary Zaccaria: a doctor who became a priest, founder of the Barnabites.

07-05.qui: Anthony Mary Zaccaria (1502-1539) was a doctor from Cremona who became a priest.
07-05.sens: He founded the Barnabites, an order of priests, and spread the Forty Hours' adoration of the Blessed Sacrament. He died at 36.
07-05.vivre: Care for bodies and for souls.

07-06: Saint Maria Goretti: an 11-year-old girl who forgave the man who killed her.

07-06.qui: Maria Goretti (1890-1902) was a poor girl from the Italian marshes.
07-06.sens: At 11 she resisted a young neighbour, Alessandro, who stabbed her; she died forgiving him. In prison Alessandro was converted; he was in Rome for her canonization in 1950, and ended his life with the Capuchins.
07-06.vivre: Forgive even what seems unforgivable, and pray for hearts to change.

07-07: Saints Ralph Milner and Roger Dickenson
An English farm labourer and a priest, martyred together in 1591.

07-07.qui: Ralph Milner was an illiterate labourer and Roger Dickenson a priest in the England of Elizabeth I, where Catholic worship was forbidden.
07-07.sens: Ralph, converted as an adult, helped the priest visit Catholics. Arrested together, they were executed at Winchester in 1591. Ralph was reportedly offered his life if he gave up his faith; he refused.

07-08: A couple of tentmakers, friends and co-workers of Saint Paul.

07-08.qui: Aquila and Priscilla were a married couple of Jewish converts, tentmakers like Saint Paul.
07-08.sens: Expelled from Rome, they welcomed Paul in Corinth and worked with him; their house served as a church (Acts 18; Rom 16:3-5). Paul says they risked their lives for him.
07-08.vivre: Open your home for a moment of prayer or friendship.

07-09: Saint Augustine Zhao Rong and companions: the martyrs of China, 120 saints canonized in 2000.

07-09.qui: Augustine Zhao Rong, a Chinese priest, and his 119 companions were martyrs in China, killed between 1648 and 1930.
07-09.sens: Among them were Chinese and European bishops and priests, but above all lay people, including children. They were canonized together in 2000.

07-10: A Benedictine monk, once page to an empress, who wrote down the customs of Cluny.

07-10.qui: Ulrich (c. 1029-1093), born in Regensburg, was page and secretary to the Empress Agnes before becoming a monk at Cluny.
07-10.sens: At the request of his friend Saint Hugh, he wrote down the customs of Cluny. He founded monasteries in Switzerland and the Black Forest, where he died blind.

07-11: The father of Western monks and patron saint of Europe.

07-11.qui: Benedict (c. 480-547), born in Nursia in Italy, left his studies in Rome to live as a hermit.
07-11.sens: He founded the monastery of Monte Cassino and wrote a Rule, full of moderation, that shapes monastic life around prayer and work: “Pray and work”. It has been followed for fifteen centuries. He is the patron saint of Europe.
07-11.vivre: Alternate work and prayer through your day.

07-12: Two soldier martyrs, honoured in Milan since Saint Ambrose.

07-12.qui: Nabor and Felix were two Christian soldiers from North Africa, martyred around 304.
07-12.sens: They were put to death at Lodi in Lombardy and buried in Milan, where Saint Ambrose praised them. 12 July is also the feast of Louis and Zélie Martin, the parents of Saint Thérèse.

07-13: A just and devout German emperor, with his wife Saint Cunegund.

07-13.qui: Henry II (973-1024) was Holy Roman Emperor.
07-13.sens: With his wife, Saint Cunegund, he ruled justly, supported Church reform and founded the diocese of Bamberg in Germany, where they are buried.
07-13.vivre: Use the responsibility you have justly.

07-14: Saint Camillus de Lellis: a former soldier and gambler who founded an order to care for the sick.

07-14.qui: Camillus de Lellis (1550-1614), a former soldier and compulsive gambler, was converted.
07-14.sens: Working as a nurse, he was shocked by how the sick were treated: he founded the Camillians, who wear a red cross on their habit. He is the patron saint of the sick and of carers.

07-15: A Franciscan theologian and biographer of Saint Francis.

07-15.qui: Bonaventure (1217-1274) was an Italian Franciscan who taught in Paris.
07-15.sens: As minister general of his order, he wrote a life of Saint Francis and books on the soul's journey to God. Made a cardinal, he died during the Council of Lyon. He is a Doctor of the Church.
07-15.vivre: Read a few lines of the life of Saint Francis.

07-16: Mary honoured by the Carmelites, on the mountain of the prophet Elijah.

07-16.qui: Mount Carmel is a mountain in Israel linked with the prophet Elijah.
07-16.sens: In the twelfth century hermits settled there and gave rise to the Carmelite order, devoted to Mary. According to tradition, Mary gave the scapular to Saint Simon Stock in 1251.

07-17.qui: Sixteen Carmelite nuns of Compiègne refused to give up religious life during the French Revolution.
07-17.sens: Sentenced to death, they climbed the scaffold in Paris one by one on 17 July 1794, singing the Veni Creator. Ten days later the Terror ended. Their story inspired Bernanos's Dialogues of the Carmelites. Pope Francis declared them saints in 2024.
07-17.vivre: Sing or pray the Veni Creator.

07-18: Saint Frederick of Utrecht: a bishop of Utrecht, martyred in the ninth century.

07-18.qui: Frederick (c. 780-838) was bishop of Utrecht, in the Netherlands.
07-18.sens: He preached the Gospel in Frisia and rebuked the empress for her conduct. He was murdered after Mass.
07-18.vivre: Have the courage to say what is right.

07-19: The eldest sister of Saint Basil and Saint Gregory of Nyssa, a model for her whole family.

07-19.qui: Macrina (c. 327-379) was the eldest of a family of saints: her brothers were Basil the Great, Gregory of Nyssa and Peter of Sebaste.
07-19.sens: After her fiancé died, she chose a consecrated life and turned the family home into a community of prayer with her mother. Her brother Gregory wrote of her life and her peaceful death.
07-19.vivre: Give thanks for a sister or brother.

07-20: A bishop of Carthage and close friend of Saint Augustine.

07-20.qui: Aurelius was bishop of Carthage from 391 to 430.
07-20.sens: He led the Church of North Africa for nearly forty years, held many councils and worked hand in hand with Saint Augustine.
07-20.vivre: Work with a friend on something useful.

07-21: Saint Lawrence of Brindisi: a Capuchin who spoke many languages, Doctor of the Church.

07-21.qui: Lawrence of Brindisi (1559-1619) was an Italian Capuchin.
07-21.sens: He spoke many languages, Hebrew among them, preached all over Europe and served as a diplomat between princes. He is a Doctor of the Church.
07-21.vivre: Learn a word or a phrase in another language.

07-22: The first to see the risen Jesus, “the apostle to the apostles”.

07-22.qui: Mary Magdalene, from Magdala on the Sea of Galilee, followed Jesus after being freed from seven demons.
07-22.sens: At the foot of the cross, and then at the tomb on Easter morning, she was the first to see the risen Jesus, who sent her to tell the apostles. That is why she is called “the apostle to the apostles”. Pope Francis raised her memorial to a feast in 2016.
07-22.vivre: Share some good news with someone.

07-23: Saint Bridget of Sweden: a mother of eight and a mystic, patron saint of Europe.

07-23.qui: Bridget (1303-1373), a Swedish noblewoman, was the mother of eight, including Saint Catherine of Sweden.
07-23.sens: As a widow she founded the Order of the Most Holy Saviour and went to Rome, where she urged the Pope to leave Avignon. She wrote down the visions she received. She is one of the patron saints of Europe.
07-23.vivre: Pray for Europe and for those who govern it.

07-24: Saint Christina the Astonishing: a mystic of Sint-Truiden, in Belgium, who prayed for the dead.

07-24.qui: Christina (1150-1224) was a poor young woman from Sint-Truiden, in today's Belgium.
07-24.sens: The accounts of her life, recorded by Cardinal Jacques de Vitry, are full of extraordinary events. She devoted her life to prayer and penance for the dead. 24 July is also the feast of Saint Charbel.
07-24.vivre: Pray for someone who has died.

07-25: The apostle venerated at Santiago de Compostela.

07-25.qui: James, son of Zebedee and brother of John, is one of the twelve apostles.
07-25.sens: A fisherman on the Sea of Galilee, he was the first apostle to be martyred, in Jerusalem around 44 (Acts 12:2). According to tradition, his relics rest at Santiago de Compostela in Galicia: since the Middle Ages pilgrims have walked there from all over Europe. He is the patron saint of Spain.
07-25.vivre: Walk for a while in prayer.

07-26: The parents of Mary, the grandparents of Jesus.

07-26.qui: According to tradition, Joachim and Anne were the parents of the Virgin Mary, and so the grandparents of Jesus.
07-26.sens: Their names come from an ancient account, the Protoevangelium of James. Since 2021 the fourth Sunday of July has been the World Day for Grandparents and the Elderly.

07-27: A married couple of Córdoba, martyred in 852.

07-27.qui: Aurelius and Natalia were a married couple in ninth-century Córdoba.
07-27.sens: Secret Christians, they eventually declared their faith openly and were martyred in 852 with three companions. They first made sure their two daughters were safe.

07-28: A monk from Wales who founded Dol in Brittany.

07-28.sens: He crossed the sea, founded the abbey of Dol in Brittany and became a bishop. He is one of the seven founding saints of Brittany, whose shrines are visited on the “Tro Breiz” pilgrimage.
07-28.vivre: Give thanks for those who founded the places of faith you go to.

07-29.qui: Martha, Mary and Lazarus were two sisters and a brother, friends of Jesus, at Bethany.
07-29.sens: Martha bustled about to welcome Jesus while Mary listened at his feet (Lk 10:38-42); when Lazarus died, Martha said “I believe that you are the Christ”, and Jesus raised his friend (Jn 11). Since 2021 the Church celebrates all three together.
07-29.vivre: Welcome someone to your table simply.

07-30: Saint Peter Chrysologus: a bishop of Ravenna with “golden words”.

07-30.qui: Peter (c. 380-450) was bishop of Ravenna, in Italy.
07-30.sens: His short, clear sermons earned him the name Chrysologus, “golden word”. He is a Doctor of the Church.
07-30.vivre: Say a few words that encourage someone.

07-31: Saint Ignatius of Loyola: a wounded soldier who founded the Jesuits and taught discernment.

07-31.qui: Ignatius (1491-1556), a Basque nobleman, was hit by a cannonball at Pamplona.
07-31.sens: While recovering he read lives of the saints and was converted. He wrote the Spiritual Exercises, which teach how to discern God's will, and founded the Society of Jesus, the Jesuits. His motto: “For the greater glory of God”.
07-31.vivre: Look back over your day in the evening: what brought me closer to God?

08-01: Saint Alphonsus Liguori: a Naples lawyer who became a priest, a gentle Doctor of the Church.

08-01.qui: Alphonsus Liguori (1696-1787) was a brilliant lawyer in Naples.
08-01.sens: After losing a case, he became a priest and preached in poor country areas. He founded the Redemptorists and wrote a great deal on moral questions, with gentleness and common sense. He is a Doctor of the Church and patron of confessors.

08-02: Saint Peter Julian Eymard: a priest from the Isère, the apostle of the Eucharist.

08-02.qui: Peter Julian Eymard (1811-1868) was a priest from La Mure, in the Isère.
08-02.sens: He founded the Congregation of the Blessed Sacrament, for adoration and to help the poor receive Communion. He has been called “the apostle of the Eucharist”.
08-02.vivre: Make a visit to the Blessed Sacrament.

08-03: The mother of the apostles James and John, who followed Jesus to the tomb.

08-03.qui: Salome was the wife of Zebedee, a fisherman on the Sea of Galilee, and the mother of the apostles James and John.
08-03.sens: She was one of the women who followed Jesus and served him. She had asked for the best places for her sons (Mt 20:20-28). She stood at the foot of the cross and on Easter morning came to the tomb with spices (Mk 16:1). That is why she is called a “myrrh-bearer”.
08-03.vivre: Stay with someone to the end.

08-04: The Curé of Ars, who spent his days hearing confessions and consoling.

08-04.qui: John Vianney (1786-1859) struggled with his studies, yet he became a priest.
08-04.sens: Sent to the little village of Ars near Lyon, he spent forty years there. He heard confessions for up to fifteen hours a day, and crowds came from all over France. He is the patron saint of parish priests.
08-04.vivre: Go to confession, or prepare to.

08-05: A monk of Lobbes who became Archbishop of Reims.

08-05.qui: Abel (died c. 764) was a Benedictine monk from the British Isles, of the abbey of Lobbes in Belgium.
08-05.sens: Pepin the Short appointed him Archbishop of Reims to reform the Church, but he had to give it up in the face of opposition and returned to Lobbes. 5 August is also the Dedication of Saint Mary Major in Rome.

08-06: On the mountain, Jesus appears in his light.

08-06.qui: Jesus takes Peter, James and John up a high mountain.
08-06.sens: He is transfigured before them: his face shines like the sun, Moses and Elijah appear, and a voice from the cloud tells them to listen to the beloved Son (Mt 17:1-9). In this way Jesus strengthens his disciples before his Passion.
08-06.vivre: Take a moment to gaze at some beautiful light.

08-07: A priest from Vicenza who staked everything on Providence.

08-07.qui: Cajetan of Thiene (1480-1547) was a priest from Vicenza.
08-07.sens: He founded the Theatines, priests who own nothing and rely on Providence. He is widely invoked in Latin America as patron of work and of bread.

08-08: The founder of the Order of Preachers, who spoke only “to God or about God”.

08-08.qui: Dominic de Guzmán (1170-1221) was a priest from Castile.
08-08.sens: Travelling in the south of France, he founded the Order of Preachers, the Dominicans, in Toulouse, to proclaim the Gospel by word and by the example of a poor life. It was said he spoke only to God or about God.

08-09: Saint Teresa Benedicta of the Cross: Edith Stein, a Jewish philosopher who became a Carmelite and died at Auschwitz.

08-09.qui: Edith Stein (1891-1942) was a German Jewish philosopher.
08-09.sens: After reading the life of Saint Teresa of Avila, she became a Catholic, then a Carmelite nun, Teresa Benedicta of the Cross. Deported by the Nazis, she died at Auschwitz. She is one of the patron saints of Europe.

08-10: Saint Lawrence, deacon of Rome, who pointed to the poor and said: “These are the treasures of the Church.”
