08-10.qui: Lawrence was one of the seven deacons of Rome, in charge of the Church's goods and of the poor.
08-10.sens: Ordered to hand over the Church's treasures, he presented the poor: “These are the treasures of the Church.” He was martyred in 258. The August shooting stars are called “the tears of Saint Lawrence”.
08-10.vivre: Watch for shooting stars and pray for the poor.

08-11: Saint Clare of Assisi: Saint Francis's friend, foundress of the Poor Clares.

08-11.qui: Clare (1194-1253), a young noblewoman of Assisi, ran away at 18 to follow Saint Francis.
08-11.sens: She founded the Order of Poor Ladies, the Poor Clares, lived at San Damiano in great poverty and was the first woman to write a rule for religious life. She is patron saint of television, because when she was ill she is said to have seen Mass on the wall of her room.

08-12: Saint Jane Frances de Chantal: a widow and mother, friend of Saint Francis de Sales.

08-12.qui: Jane Frances de Chantal (1572-1641), a Burgundian baroness, was widowed at 28 with four children.
08-12.sens: Guided by Saint Francis de Sales, she founded with him the Order of the Visitation, open to women in frail health. She was the grandmother of Madame de Sévigné.
08-12.vivre: Write a friend a word of support.

08-13: A pope and a priest, opponents reconciled in exile.

08-13.qui: Pontian, the pope, and Hippolytus, a Roman priest, had been at odds: Hippolytus had even been an antipope.
08-13.sens: Both were deported to the mines of Sardinia around 235, and they were reconciled there before they died. The Church celebrates them together.
08-13.vivre: Take the first step towards making peace.

08-14: Saint Maximilian Kolbe: a Franciscan who took a father's place at Auschwitz.

08-14.qui: Maximilian Kolbe (1894-1941) was a Polish Franciscan who founded Catholic newspapers.
08-14.sens: Deported to Auschwitz, he took the place of a family man condemned to starve to death, and died after two weeks in the bunker. John Paul II canonized him in 1982 as a “martyr of charity”.
08-14.vivre: Take on a burden for someone who is tired.

08-15: Mary enters, body and soul, into the glory of God.

08-15.qui: At the end of her earthly life, Mary was taken up body and soul into the glory of God.
08-15.sens: This is the Assumption, a dogma proclaimed by Pius XII in 1950 but celebrated since the early centuries. Mary is the first to live fully the resurrection promised to everyone. In many countries it is celebrated with processions.
08-15.vivre: Pray to Mary for your country.

08-16: A monk from Britain who founded a monastery in Brittany.

08-16.qui: Armel (sixth century) was a Breton monk from Britain who crossed the sea with the emigrants.
08-16.sens: He founded a monastery at Plouarmel in Brittany. According to legend, he tamed a dragon with his stole. 16 August is also the feast of Saint Roch.

08-17: Saint Clare of Montefalco: an Augustinian abbess in Umbria, centred on the cross of Christ.

08-17.qui: Clare (1268-1308) joined her sister's community at Montefalco, in Umbria, as a young girl.
08-17.sens: As abbess she begged for her poor community and counselled everyone who came to her. She meditated constantly on the Passion of Jesus. She was canonized in 1881.
08-17.vivre: Look at a cross and say thank you.

08-18: The mother of the Emperor Constantine, who went on pilgrimage to Jerusalem.

08-18.qui: Helena (c. 248-329) was the mother of the Emperor Constantine.
08-18.sens: As a Christian she made a pilgrimage to the Holy Land and had basilicas built in Bethlehem and on the Mount of Olives. According to tradition, she found the cross of Christ in Jerusalem.
08-18.vivre: Spend a quiet moment before a cross.

08-19: Saint John Eudes: a Norman priest and missionary, apostle of the Hearts of Jesus and Mary.

08-19.qui: John Eudes (1601-1680) was a priest from Normandy.
08-19.sens: A tireless missionary, he preached in the countryside, founded seminaries to train priests and a congregation to shelter women in distress. He was the first to have a feast of the Heart of Jesus celebrated.
08-19.vivre: Pray to the Heart of Jesus.

08-20: Saint Bernard of Clairvaux: a Burgundian monk who sang Mary's praises.

08-20.qui: Bernard (1090-1153), a Burgundian nobleman, entered Cîteaux with thirty companions.
08-20.sens: He founded the abbey of Clairvaux, from which dozens of others were founded. A great preacher and adviser to popes, he wrote magnificent texts about Mary. The prayer “Remember, O most gracious Virgin Mary” (the Memorare) is attributed to him.

08-21: The pope who opened Communion to young children.

08-21.qui: Pius X (1835-1914), Giuseppe Sarto, son of a postman in the Veneto, was pope from 1903 to 1914.
08-21.sens: He allowed children to receive Communion from the age of reason, encouraged frequent Communion and reformed sacred music. He died at the start of the First World War.
08-21.vivre: Help a child prepare for First Communion.

08-22: A week after the Assumption, Mary crowned queen.

08-22.qui: A week after the Assumption, the Church celebrates Mary as Queen.
08-22.sens: Pius XII instituted this feast in 1954. Mary is queen not in the manner of the powerful, but as a servant, mother of the King who made himself a servant.

08-23: Saint Rose of Lima: the first saint of the Americas, who cared for the poor at home.

08-23.qui: Rose of Lima (1586-1617) was a young woman in Peru.
08-23.sens: A member of the Dominican Third Order, she lived in prayer and cared for the poor and sick in her parents' home. She is the first saint of the American continent and patron saint of Latin America.

08-24: The apostle Jesus saw under the fig tree.

08-24.qui: Bartholomew is one of the twelve apostles, often identified with Nathanael.
08-24.sens: Jesus saw him under the fig tree and said of him: “Here is truly an Israelite in whom there is no deceit” (Jn 1:47). According to tradition, he brought the Gospel to Armenia and was martyred there. In France this day also recalls the Saint Bartholomew's Day massacre of 1572.

08-25: Saint Louis, King of France, who served the poor at his own table.

08-25.qui: Louis IX (1214-1270) was King of France.
08-25.sens: He dispensed justice under an oak tree at Vincennes, served the poor at his own table himself and had the Sainte-Chapelle built. He died of illness in Tunis during a crusade. He is a patron saint of France.

08-26: Saint Caesarius of Arles: a bishop of Arles, a great preacher who protected the people during the invasions.

08-26.qui: Caesarius (c. 470-542), from Burgundy, was a monk at Lérins and then bishop of Arles for forty years.
08-26.sens: He preached simply so that everyone could understand, ransomed prisoners by selling the sacred vessels, and wrote the first rule for nuns, for the monastery founded for his sister.
08-26.vivre: Explain something about your faith simply.

08-27: The mother who prayed for years for her son Augustine.

08-27.qui: Monica (331-387), born in North Africa, was the mother of Saint Augustine.
08-27.sens: For years she prayed and wept for the conversion of her son, who was living a wild life. A bishop told her: “It is impossible that the son of so many tears should be lost.” She died soon after Augustine's baptism. She is the patron saint of mothers.
08-27.vivre: Pray for a child, with trust.

08-28: Saint Augustine of Hippo: “You have made us for yourself, and our heart is restless until it rests in you.”

08-28.qui: Augustine (354-430), born in North Africa, was a brilliant teacher who searched for truth everywhere.
08-28.sens: In Milan, moved by Saint Ambrose and his mother's prayers, he was converted at 32. As bishop of Hippo he wrote the Confessions and The City of God. In them he says to God: “You have made us for yourself, and our heart is restless until it rests in you.” He is a Doctor of the Church.
08-28.vivre: Let your heart rest in God for a few moments.

08-29: The Passion of Saint John the Baptist
John the Baptist dies for telling the truth.

08-29.qui: John the Baptist denounced King Herod Antipas's marriage to his brother's wife.
08-29.sens: Imprisoned, he was beheaded at Herodias's request after her daughter's dance (Mk 6:17-29). He died for telling the truth.
08-29.vivre: Tell the truth with courage and charity.

08-30: A hermit from Ireland, near Meaux, patron saint of gardeners.

08-30.qui: Fiacre was a hermit who came from Ireland in the seventh century.
08-30.sens: The bishop of Meaux gave him land in the forest at Breuil, where he grew a garden to feed the poor and pilgrims. He is the patron saint of gardeners. Paris's horse-drawn cabs, “fiacres”, were named after an inn sign bearing his image. 30 August is also Saint Jeanne Jugan's day.

08-31: A converted Athenian philosopher who wrote to the emperor in defence of Christians.

08-31.qui: Aristides was a philosopher of Athens in the second century.
08-31.sens: After his conversion he sent the Emperor Hadrian an apology, one of the oldest Christian writings after the New Testament, describing how Christians live: they love their enemies and help widows and orphans.
08-31.vivre: Live in a way that makes the Gospel believable.

09-01: A hermit of Provence who protected a doe, according to legend. It is also the day of prayer for Creation.

09-01.qui: Giles was a seventh-century hermit, from Greece according to tradition, who settled near the Rhône.
09-01.sens: It is said he lived on the milk of a doe and was wounded by a hunter's arrow while protecting her. The abbey of Saint-Gilles in the Camargue was a major stop on the way to Compostela. Since 2015, 1 September has also been the World Day of Prayer for the Care of Creation.

09-02: A Swedish noblewoman who founded Sweden's first convent of Dominican nuns.

09-02.qui: Ingrid (died 1282) was a Swedish noblewoman, granddaughter of a king.
09-02.sens: As a widow she went on pilgrimage to the Holy Land and Rome, then founded a Dominican convent at Skänninge in Sweden, where she died.
09-02.vivre: Make a small pilgrimage near where you live.

09-03: Saint Gregory the Great: a pope who called himself “servant of the servants of God”.

09-03.qui: Gregory (c. 540-604), prefect of Rome, became a monk and then pope in 590.
09-03.sens: He fed Rome during famines, sent missionaries to England and wrote a great deal. He called himself “servant of the servants of God”. Gregorian chant is named after him. He is a Doctor of the Church.

09-04: A hermit of Palermo, patron saint of the city.

09-04.qui: Rosalia (c. 1130-1170) was a young Sicilian noblewoman who withdrew to live as a hermit in a cave on Mount Pellegrino.
09-04.sens: In 1624, during a plague in Palermo, her remains were found and the epidemic ended. She is the patron saint of Palermo, where her feast is celebrated with great fervour.
09-04.vivre: Pray for those suffering in an epidemic.

09-05: A young Egyptian martyr who chose to join the Christians under arrest.

09-05.qui: Rhais, or Irais, was a young woman in Egypt, martyred in the early fourth century.
09-05.sens: On her way to draw water, she saw monks and consecrated virgins being led away for their faith; she joined them and was martyred at Antinoe. 5 September is also the feast of Saint Teresa of Calcutta.
09-05.vivre: Stand beside someone who is suffering.

09-06: Blessed Bertrand of Garrigues: one of Saint Dominic's first companions.

09-06.qui: Bertrand (died c. 1230) was born at Garrigues, in the Gard.
09-06.sens: He followed Saint Dominic and became one of the first Friars Preachers; Dominic sent him to found the friary in Paris, near the university. He was known for weeping over other people's sins as over his own.
09-06.vivre: Pray for those who proclaim the Gospel.

09-07: A young martyr of Burgundy, venerated at Alise-Sainte-Reine.

09-07.qui: According to tradition, Regina was a young shepherdess of Alesia in Burgundy, martyred in the third century.
09-07.sens: She refused to marry the Roman governor and died for her faith. The village of Alise-Sainte-Reine holds a procession in her honour every year.
09-07.vivre: Pray for young women who have to say no.

09-08: The birth of the mother of Jesus.

09-08.qui: Nine months after the Immaculate Conception, the Church celebrates the birth of Mary.
09-08.sens: According to tradition, her parents were Joachim and Anne. It is one of only three births celebrated in the liturgical year, with those of Jesus and John the Baptist.
09-08.vivre: Wish Mary a happy birthday with a Hail Mary.

09-09: Saint Peter Claver: a Catalan Jesuit, “the slave of the slaves” in Cartagena de Indias.

09-09.qui: Peter Claver (1580-1654), a Catalan Jesuit, went to Cartagena de Indias, in Colombia.
09-09.sens: In that great slave-trading port, for forty years he met enslaved Africans as they arrived, nursed them, fed them and baptized them. He signed himself “slave of the slaves for ever”.
09-09.vivre: Find out about a form of modern slavery.

09-10: Blessed Agnes Takeya: a Japanese widow martyred at Nagasaki for sheltering missionaries.

09-10.qui: Agnes Takeya was a Japanese widow of forty-five.
09-10.sens: For hiding missionaries, she was beheaded at Nagasaki on 10 September 1622 with other Christians, in Japan's “Great Martyrdom”.
09-10.vivre: Open your door to someone who needs shelter.

09-11: Saint Theodora of Alexandria: a woman of Alexandria who did penance all her life.

09-11.qui: According to an ancient account, Theodora (fifth century) was a married woman of Alexandria.
09-11.sens: After a fault, full of remorse, she entered a monastery disguised as a man, accepted being falsely accused and raised the child attributed to her. The truth came out at her death. A story about forgiveness and humility.

09-12: The Most Holy Name of Mary
We celebrate the name of Mary, borne by so many Christians.

09-12.qui: On 12 September the Church celebrates the name of Mary.
09-12.sens: The feast was extended to the whole Church in 1683, after the victory at Vienna, which was attributed to prayer. Mary, Miriam in Hebrew, is the most common name among Christian women all over the world.
09-12.vivre: Pray for everyone who bears the name Mary.

09-13: Saint John Chrysostom: a bishop of Constantinople with a “golden mouth”.

09-13.qui: John (c. 349-407), a priest of Antioch, became Archbishop of Constantinople.
09-13.sens: His sermons were so beautiful that he was called Chrysostom, “golden mouth”. He denounced the luxury of the court and defended the poor; he died in exile. He is a Doctor of the Church.

09-14: The Exaltation of the Holy Cross
The cross, a sign of death that became a sign of love.

09-14.qui: According to tradition, Saint Helena found the cross of Christ in Jerusalem; the Basilica of the Holy Sepulchre was consecrated on 14 September 335.
09-14.sens: We celebrate the cross not as an instrument of death but as the sign of God's love, which gives its life. “God so loved the world” (Jn 3:16).
09-14.vivre: Make the sign of the cross slowly.

09-15: Mary standing at the foot of the cross.

09-15.qui: The day after the Holy Cross, the Church celebrates Mary standing at the foot of the cross.
09-15.sens: We meditate on her seven sorrows, from Simeon's prophecy to the burial. The Stabat Mater, “At the cross her station keeping”, is sung on this day.
09-15.vivre: Pray for a mother who is suffering.

09-16: A pope and a bishop of Carthage, friends and martyrs.

09-16.qui: Cornelius, pope (251-253), and Cyprian, bishop of Carthage, were friends despite the distance between them.
09-16.sens: Both upheld that Christians who had denied the faith during persecution and repented should be welcomed back with mercy. Both died as martyrs, Cornelius in exile and Cyprian beheaded in 258.
09-16.vivre: Welcome back someone who returns, with mercy.

09-17: Saint Hildegard of Bingen: a German abbess, musician, scholar and Doctor of the Church.

09-17.qui: Hildegard (1098-1179) was a Benedictine abbess at Bingen, in Germany.
09-17.sens: A visionary and musician, she composed chants, wrote about plants and medicine, and corresponded with popes and emperors. She was proclaimed a Doctor of the Church in 2012.
09-17.vivre: Listen to some music by Hildegard of Bingen.

09-18: Saint Joseph of Cupertino: a simple friar who struggled at school, patron of students sitting exams.

09-18.qui: Joseph of Cupertino (1603-1663) was a Franciscan friar from Apulia.
09-18.sens: Not gifted at studies, he nevertheless passed the exam to become a priest by being asked the only questions he knew. He is the patron saint of students taking exams. It is reported that he went into ecstasy during prayer.
09-18.vivre: Entrust an upcoming exam or test to God.

09-19: A martyred bishop, patron saint of Naples.

09-19.qui: Januarius was bishop of Benevento, martyred around 305.
09-19.sens: He is the patron saint of Naples, where a vial of his blood is kept: three times a year, crowds wait for it to liquefy, which they see as a sign of protection for the city.
09-19.vivre: Pray for Naples and for your own town.

09-20: Saint Andrew Kim and companions: the martyrs of Korea, whose Church was born of lay people.

09-20.qui: Andrew Kim Taegon (1821-1846), the first Korean priest, and Paul Chong Hasang, a layman, were martyred with one hundred and one companions.
09-20.sens: The Church in Korea was born in the eighteenth century from lay people who had discovered the faith in books, without missionaries. They were canonized in 1984 by John Paul II in Seoul.
09-20.vivre: Give thanks for lay people who pass on the faith.

09-21: The tax collector Jesus called to his table.

09-21.qui: Matthew was a tax collector in Capernaum, a despised trade.
09-21.sens: Jesus said to him “Follow me”, and he got up (Mt 9:9). He held a meal for Jesus with other sinners. Tradition credits him with the first Gospel. His symbol is a winged man.
09-21.vivre: Invite someone you think of as different from you.

09-22: An officer of the Theban Legion, martyred at Agaunum, in Switzerland.

09-22.qui: Maurice was the commander of the Theban Legion, which came from Egypt.
09-22.sens: According to tradition, he and his soldiers refused to massacre Christians and were put to death at Agaunum, in Switzerland, around 287. The abbey of Saint-Maurice, founded over their tomb in 515, is the oldest monastery in the West still in use.
09-22.vivre: Refuse to do harm, even if ordered to.

09-23: Saint Pio of Pietrelcina: Padre Pio, a Capuchin who heard the confessions of crowds.

09-23.qui: Pio of Pietrelcina (1887-1968) was an Italian Capuchin, Padre Pio.
09-23.sens: At San Giovanni Rotondo he spent long hours hearing confessions and drew huge crowds. For fifty years he bore the stigmata, wounds like those of Christ. He founded a large hospital, the Home for the Relief of Suffering. He was canonized in 2002.
09-23.vivre: Pray for people suffering in hospital.

09-24: A Russian monk of Mount Athos who prayed for the whole world.

09-24.qui: Silouan (1866-1938), a Russian peasant with a violent temper, was converted at 26.
09-24.sens: He became a monk on Mount Athos and lived there for forty-six years. He left writings on love of enemies and humility. The Orthodox Church canonized him in 1987. 24 September is also the feast of Our Lady of Mercy, patroness of Barcelona.
09-24.vivre: Pray for someone who has hurt you.

09-25: The first bishop of Amiens, born in Pamplona according to tradition.

09-25.qui: According to tradition, Firmin was born in Pamplona, in Navarre, and baptized by Saint Saturninus.
09-25.sens: He became a bishop and was martyred at Amiens, whose first bishop he was. His life is carved on the portal of Amiens Cathedral; in Pamplona, the San Fermín festival is held in July.
09-25.vivre: Pray for the town where you live.

09-26: Twin doctors who treated people without charging.

09-26.qui: Cosmas and Damian were twin brothers and doctors, martyred in Syria around 300.
09-26.sens: They treated people for free: they were called the “Anargyroi”, those who refuse money. They are the patron saints of doctors and pharmacists. Their names are mentioned in the Eucharistic Prayer at Mass.
09-26.vivre: Thank your doctor or a carer.

09-27: Saint Vincent de Paul: the priest of charity, serving the poor of France.

09-27.qui: Vincent de Paul (1581-1660), the son of farmers in the Landes, became a priest in search of a comfortable life.
09-27.sens: Moved by poverty, he changed his life: he founded the Vincentians to preach in the countryside and, with Louise de Marillac, the Daughters of Charity. He organized relief for the poor, abandoned children and galley slaves. He is the patron saint of charitable works.
09-27.vivre: Give something to a charity you trust.

09-28: A Duke of Bohemia, patron saint of the Czechs.

09-28.sens: A just Christian prince, he was murdered by his brother on his way to Mass. He is the patron saint of the Czech Republic; the English carol Good King Wenceslas tells of his charity.
09-28.vivre: Do a quiet act of charity.

09-29.qui: The Church celebrates the three archangels whom the Bible names.
09-29.sens: Michael, “Who is like God?”, fights evil. Gabriel, “Strength of God”, announces to Mary the birth of Jesus. Raphael, “God heals”, travels with young Tobias. In England this day is Michaelmas.
09-29.vivre: Ask Saint Michael to protect you from evil.

09-30: The scholar who translated the Bible into Latin: “Ignorance of Scripture is ignorance of Christ.”

09-30.qui: Jerome (c. 347-420), born in Dalmatia, was a scholar with a difficult temper.
09-30.sens: At Pope Damasus's request, he translated the Bible into Latin from Hebrew and Greek: the Vulgate, used for more than a thousand years. He spent his last years in Bethlehem. He said: “Ignorance of Scripture is ignorance of Christ.” He is the patron saint of translators.
09-30.vivre: Read a chapter of the Bible.

10-01: Saint Thérèse of the Child Jesus: the “little way” of trust, patron saint of missions.

10-01.qui: Thérèse Martin (1873-1897), youngest daughter of Louis and Zélie Martin, entered the Carmel of Lisieux at 15.
10-01.sens: She died of tuberculosis at 24. Her autobiography, Story of a Soul, made known her “little way”: a child's trust in God. She is a Doctor of the Church and patron saint of missions, though she never left her convent.
10-01.vivre: Do a little thing with great love.

10-02: Everyone has an angel who watches over them.

10-02.qui: On 2 October the Church celebrates the guardian angels.
10-02.sens: She believes that from birth each person has an angel who watches over and guides them (Catechism, no. 336). Jesus says of children that their angels always see the face of the Father (Mt 18:10).

10-03: Saint Gerard of Brogne: a former knight who became a monk and reformed abbeys.

10-03.qui: Gerard (c. 895-959) was a nobleman of the county of Namur, first a man of arms.
10-03.sens: He became a Benedictine, founded the abbey of Brogne on his lands, and then reformed many abbeys in Flanders and Lorraine. On the evening of 3 October Franciscans also remember the death of Saint Francis.
10-03.vivre: Put some part of your life back in order.

10-04: Saint Francis of Assisi: the poor man of Assisi, brother of all Creation.

10-04.qui: Francis (1182-1226), son of a rich Assisi merchant, dreamed of becoming a knight.
10-04.sens: After an illness and an encounter with a leper, he gave up everything and lived in poverty, joy and praise. He founded the Friars Minor, received the stigmata and composed the Canticle of the Creatures. He is patron saint of Italy and of ecology.
10-04.vivre: Thank God for one of his creatures: the sun, water, an animal.

10-05: A Polish nun, messenger of God's mercy.

10-05.qui: Faustina Kowalska (1905-1938) was a Polish nun from a very simple background.
10-05.sens: She received messages from Jesus about his mercy, which she wrote in her Diary, and had the image “Jesus, I trust in you” painted. John Paul II canonized her in 2000 and instituted Divine Mercy Sunday.

10-06: A teacher from Reims who went into the wilderness of Chartreuse.

10-06.qui: Bruno (c. 1030-1101), born in Cologne, was a renowned teacher in Reims.
10-06.sens: In 1084 he went with six companions into the wilderness of Chartreuse, near Grenoble: the origin of the Carthusians, who live in silence and solitude. The Grande Chartreuse is still inhabited.
10-06.vivre: Keep a real moment of silence.

10-07: The rosary, a prayer for young and old.

10-07.qui: On 7 October the Church celebrates Our Lady of the Rosary.
10-07.sens: The feast began after the victory of Lepanto in 1571, attributed to the praying of the rosary that Pope Pius V had asked for. The rosary meditates on the mysteries of Jesus' life with Mary. October is the month of the rosary.
10-07.vivre: Pray a decade of the rosary.

10-08: A famous actress of Antioch who converted and ended her life as a hermit in Jerusalem.

10-08.qui: Pelagia was a celebrated actress and dancer of Antioch in the fifth century.
10-08.sens: Moved by a bishop's preaching, she was converted, gave away her fortune and went to live as a hermit on the Mount of Olives in Jerusalem, disguised as a monk.

10-09: The first bishop of Paris, martyred at Montmartre.

10-09.qui: Denis was the first bishop of Paris, in the third century.
10-09.sens: According to tradition, he was beheaded at Montmartre, the “mount of martyrs”, with his companions Rusticus and Eleutherius; legend says he walked, carrying his head, to the place of his burial. The Basilica of Saint-Denis, where the kings of France lie, is built over his tomb.
10-09.vivre: Pray for Paris and for France.

10-10: Saint Daniel and companions: seven Franciscan friars martyred at Ceuta in 1227.

10-10.qui: Daniel and six other Franciscans, six of them priests, landed at Ceuta, in Morocco, in 1227.
10-10.sens: They preached Christ, were arrested and beheaded. The night before they died, Daniel washed his companions' feet, as Jesus did before his Passion. 10 October is also the feast of Saint Daniel Comboni.
10-10.vivre: Do a humble service for those close to you.

10-11: Saint Theophanes the Hymnographer: a monk of Palestine branded for defending icons.

10-11.qui: Theophanes (c. 778-845) was a monk of the monastery of Saint Sabbas, near Jerusalem.
10-11.sens: During the iconoclast crisis he was tortured and branded on the forehead for defending the veneration of images. As bishop of Nicaea he composed many hymns. 11 October is also the feast of Saint John XXIII.
10-11.vivre: Pray before an icon or holy image.

10-12: A young woman of Quercy, patron saint of Saint-Céré.

10-12.qui: Speria, or Esperia (eighth century), was born in Quercy.
10-12.sens: She refused marriage to consecrate herself to God and lived as a hermit; according to tradition she was killed by her brother. The town of Saint-Céré, in the Lot, bears her name. 12 October is also the feast of Our Lady of the Pillar, patroness of the Hispanic world and Spain's National Day.
10-12.vivre: Respect the life choices of someone close to you.

10-13: A count of Auvergne, a just and generous layman, founder of the abbey of Aurillac.

10-13.qui: Gerald (855-909) was Count of Aurillac, in Auvergne.
10-13.sens: A layman, he governed his lands justly, freed his serfs and founded the abbey of Aurillac. His life, written by Saint Odo of Cluny, was the first to present a layman as a model of holiness. 13 October 1917 is also the day of the “miracle of the sun” at Fatima.

10-14: A former slave who became pope in the third century.

10-14.qui: Callistus, a former slave, became pope in 217.
10-14.sens: He organized the cemetery on the Appian Way, the catacombs that bear his name, and showed mercy to repentant sinners. He was martyred around 222.
10-14.vivre: Visit a cemetery and pray for the dead.

10-15: Saint Teresa of Avila: a Carmelite of Castile who spoke to God as a friend.

10-15.qui: Teresa (1515-1582), a Carmelite of Avila in Castile, reformed the Carmelites and founded seventeen convents.
10-15.sens: She described prayer as a friendly conversation with God and wrote The Interior Castle. Full of humour and energy, she was the first woman proclaimed a Doctor of the Church, in 1970. She died on the night of 4 to 15 October 1582, the night the Gregorian calendar came in.
10-15.vivre: Talk to God as a friend for five minutes.

10-16: A nun of Paray-le-Monial, confidante of the Heart of Jesus.

10-16.qui: Margaret Mary Alacoque (1647-1690) was a Visitation nun at Paray-le-Monial.
10-16.sens: Jesus revealed to her his Heart “which has so loved mankind” and asked for a feast in its honour. Supported by Saint Claude de la Colombière, she spread devotion to the Sacred Heart. Paray-le-Monial is a major place of pilgrimage.
10-16.vivre: Pray to the Heart of Jesus.

10-17: Saint Ignatius of Antioch: a bishop who wrote seven letters on his way to martyrdom in Rome.

10-17.qui: Ignatius was bishop of Antioch, in Syria, at the end of the first century.
10-17.sens: Condemned to the beasts, he was taken to Rome and on the way wrote seven letters to the Churches, speaking of the Eucharist and of unity. He is one of the first to use the expression “Catholic Church”.
10-17.vivre: Pray for unity in your parish.

10-18: The doctor who wrote a Gospel and the Acts of the Apostles.

10-18.qui: Luke, a Greek doctor and companion of Saint Paul, wrote a Gospel and the Acts of the Apostles.
10-18.sens: His Gospel, the Gospel of mercy, is the only one to tell the parables of the prodigal son and the good Samaritan, and the childhood of Jesus from Mary's side. A tradition says he painted the Virgin; he is patron saint of doctors and artists.
10-18.vivre: Read the parable of the prodigal son (Lk 15).

10-19: John de Brébeuf, Isaac Jogues and their companions, French missionaries.

10-19.qui: John de Brébeuf, Isaac Jogues and six companions were French Jesuits and laymen, missionaries among the Huron and Iroquois.
10-19.sens: They were martyred between 1642 and 1649, in today's Canada and New York State. Brébeuf had written a Christmas carol in the Huron language. They were canonized in 1930.
10-19.vivre: Pray for the peoples of Canada.

10-20: The first abbess of the “White Ladies” of Mortain.

10-20.qui: Adeline (died 1125) was the sister of Saint Vitalis, abbot of Savigny in Normandy.
10-20.sens: She founded a community of nuns near Mortain; they were called the “White Ladies” because of their Cistercian habit.
10-20.vivre: Give thanks for a brother or sister who has helped you.

10-21: The mother of Saint Remigius, the bishop who baptized Clovis.

10-21.qui: Celine was the mother of Saint Remigius, in the fifth century.
10-21.sens: According to tradition, she had this son late in life, as a hermit had foretold. She died at Cerny, in the Aisne. 21 October is also the day of Saint Ursula and her companions, martyrs of Cologne.

10-22: Two Spanish sisters martyred in the ninth century.

10-22.qui: Nunilo and Alodia were two sisters from Huesca, in Aragon, born to a Muslim father and a Christian mother.
10-22.sens: They refused to give up their Christian faith and were martyred in 851. 22 October is also the feast of Saint John Paul II.
10-22.vivre: Pray for a sister, a brother or a friend.

10-23: Saint John of Capistrano: an Italian lawyer who became a Franciscan and a great preacher.

10-23.qui: John of Capistrano (1386-1456), a lawyer and governor of Perugia, became a Franciscan after a spell in prison.
10-23.sens: A great preacher, he travelled all over Europe. He died of plague after the defence of Belgrade. He is the patron saint of military chaplains.
10-23.vivre: Pray for those who serve in the armed forces.

10-24: A monk from Scotland, venerated in Lorraine.

10-24.qui: Florentinus was a seventh-century monk from Scotland who settled at Bonnet, in the Meuse.
10-24.sens: Little is known of him except that people came on pilgrimage to his tomb; the church at Bonnet shows him tending pigs. 24 October is also the feast of Saint Anthony Mary Claret.
10-24.vivre: Do your daily work humbly and well.

10-25: Two shoemaker brothers of Soissons, patron saints of shoemakers.

10-25.qui: Crispin and Crispinian were two Roman brothers who came to evangelize Soissons in the third century.
10-25.sens: They worked as shoemakers, making shoes for the poor without charging, and died as martyrs. They are the patron saints of shoemakers. In Shakespeare's Henry V, the battle of Agincourt is fought on Saint Crispin's Day.
10-25.vivre: Do someone a service with the skills you have.

10-26: A martyr of Thessalonica, much loved by Eastern Christians.

10-26.qui: Demetrius was a deacon or an officer martyred at Thessalonica around 306.
10-26.sens: He is one of the most venerated saints of the Christian East, patron of Thessalonica, where a great basilica houses his tomb.
10-26.vivre: Pray for the Christians of the East.

10-27: A Cistercian nun in Champagne in the twelfth century.

10-27.qui: Emeline (died 1178) lived as a recluse at the Cistercian monastery of Boulancourt, in the Haute-Marne.
10-27.sens: Little is known of her hidden life of prayer. 27 October also recalls the great day of prayer for peace that John Paul II held in Assisi in 1986.
10-27.vivre: Pray for peace in the world.

10-28: Two apostles who went to proclaim the Gospel in the East.

10-28.qui: Simon, called the Zealot, and Jude, also called Thaddeus, are two of the twelve apostles.
10-28.sens: According to tradition, they preached the Gospel in Persia and were martyred there. Jude is invoked in desperate cases; a letter in the New Testament bears his name.
10-28.vivre: Entrust a difficult situation to Saint Jude.

10-29: A bishop, patron saint of Girona, in Catalonia.

10-29.qui: According to Catalan tradition, Narcissus was a bishop of Girona, martyred in the fourth century.
10-29.sens: He is the patron saint of Girona, where it is said that flies swarming from his tomb drove off French invaders in 1285. The Fira de Sant Narcís is the city's great festival. Another Saint Narcissus, a second-century bishop of Jerusalem, is also celebrated on this day.
10-29.vivre: Find out who the patron saint of your town is.

10-30: A laywoman of Friuli, a Dominican tertiary.

10-30.qui: Benvenuta Bojani (1255-1292) was a young woman of Friuli, in Italy.
10-30.sens: She lived her faith at home, without entering a convent, in the Third Order of Saint Dominic, with great devotion to the Passion of Christ.
10-30.vivre: Live your faith where you are, at home.

10-31: A young Roman who came to evangelize Picardy and was martyred.

10-31.qui: According to tradition, Quentin was a young Roman who came to evangelize Picardy in the third century.
10-31.sens: He was martyred at Augusta Viromanduorum, the town that took his name: Saint-Quentin, in the Aisne. 31 October is also the eve of All Saints' Day.
10-31.vivre: Get ready for the feast of All Saints.

11-01: The feast of all the saints, known and unknown.
11-02: We pray for all who have died.
11-03: The bishop of Liège, patron saint of hunters, foresters and the Ardennes.

11-03.qui: Hubert lived in the eighth century. According to tradition, he was a young nobleman passionate about hunting; after his wife's death he changed his life, became a priest, then bishop of Maastricht and Liège, where he brought the Gospel to the Ardennes. He died in 727.
11-03.sens: Legend says that one day while hunting he saw a stag with a shining cross between its antlers and heard Christ calling him. He is celebrated on 3 November, the day his relics were moved in 743. That is why hunters and foresters took him as their patron: Saint Hubert Masses are still celebrated with hunting horns, and animals are blessed.
11-03.vivre: Take a walk in the woods and thank God for nature and the animals he entrusts to us.

11-04: Saint Charles Borromeo: an archbishop of Milan who stayed with the sick during the plague.

11-04.qui: Charles Borromeo (1538-1584), a pope's nephew, became Archbishop of Milan very young. Instead of enjoying his rank, he reformed his diocese and opened seminaries and catechism schools.
11-04.sens: When plague struck Milan in 1576, many nobles fled; he stayed, nursed the sick and sold his possessions to feed the city. He is celebrated on 4 November, the day after his death.
11-04.vivre: Do something practical for someone going through a hard time, without waiting to be asked.

11-05: The first abbess of Chelles, chosen by Queen Bathilde.

11-05.qui: Bertilla (c. 630-705) was a nun at Jouarre, in Brie.
11-05.sens: Queen Saint Bathilde chose her as the first abbess of Chelles, near Paris. For forty-six years she led a large community, which even drew young women from England. 5 November is also the memorial of Zechariah and Elizabeth, the parents of John the Baptist.
11-05.vivre: Be faithful in the small things of every day.

11-06: Saint Leonard of Noblat: a hermit of the Limousin, patron saint of prisoners.

11-06.qui: Leonard, in the sixth century, was a Frankish nobleman baptized by Saint Remigius. He refused honours and withdrew as a hermit to Noblat, near Limoges.
11-06.sens: It is said he obtained the release of prisoners and took them in; he became the patron saint of prisoners, and chains were left as offerings in his church at Saint-Léonard-de-Noblat.
11-06.vivre: Think of someone “locked in” by loneliness or hardship, and get in touch.

11-07: A martyr of Ankara who died with her husband and son.

11-07.qui: Karina, her husband Melasippus and their son Antony were Christians of Ankara, in today's Turkey, in the fourth century.
11-07.sens: Under the Emperor Julian, the couple were tortured in front of their son, who did not deny his faith and died in his turn. On this day we also celebrate Saint Willibrord, apostle of the Netherlands, and Saint Ernest, a German abbot.

11-08: Saint Godfrey of Amiens: an abbot who became bishop of Amiens and defended ordinary people.

11-08.qui: Godfrey (c. 1066-1115) was abbot of Nogent-sous-Coucy in Picardy, a monastery he revived when only a few monks were left.
11-08.sens: As bishop of Amiens, he supported the townspeople against the abuses of the lords. 8 November is also the feast of Saint Elizabeth of the Trinity. In the Orthodox Churches it is the feast of Saint Michael the Archangel and all the angels (the “Synaxis of the Archangels”); those that still follow the old Julian calendar celebrate it on 21 November.

11-09: The Dedication of the Lateran Basilica
The Pope's cathedral, “mother of all churches”.
11-10: Saint Leo the Great: the pope who faced Attila at the gates of Rome.

11-10.qui: Leo the Great was pope from 440 to 461, as the Roman Empire was collapsing.
11-10.sens: In 452 he went out to meet Attila, who was threatening Rome, and persuaded him to withdraw. He also wrote very clear letters and sermons on Jesus, true God and true man. He is celebrated on 10 November, the day of his death.
11-10.vivre: Dare to speak a word of peace in a tense situation.

11-11: Saint Martin of Tours: the soldier who shared his cloak with a beggar.

11-11.qui: Martin (c. 316-397) was a Roman soldier born in Hungary. One winter's day in Amiens, he cut his cloak in two for a beggar shivering in the cold; the next night he saw Christ in a dream, wearing that piece of cloak.
11-11.sens: He was baptized, became a monk and then bishop of Tours, and travelled the countryside of Gaul. He is one of the most popular saints in Europe: thousands of villages and churches bear his name. 11 November is also Armistice Day, recalling the end of the First World War in 1918.
11-11.vivre: Share something warm: clothes, a meal, some time.

11-12: A bishop in today's Belarus, martyr for Christian unity.

11-12.qui: Josaphat Kuntsevych (c. 1580-1623) was a monk and then Archbishop of Polotsk, in today's Belarus.
11-12.sens: An Eastern-rite Christian in union with Rome, he worked all his life for unity between Catholics and Orthodox. He was killed in 1623 amid violent tensions. He is celebrated on 12 November, the day of his death.
11-12.vivre: Pray for Christian unity, and for someone you have fallen out with.

11-13: Saint Martin's successor at Tours, long a troublemaker before he changed his ways.

11-13.qui: Brice (c. 370-444) was a young cleric trained by Saint Martin at Tours. He was proud and quarrelsome and gave his master plenty of trouble.
11-13.sens: Martin is said to have foretold that Brice would nevertheless succeed him, and so he did. A contested bishop, exiled for a time, he gradually changed and returned to Tours, where he died in peace. A saint who shows that nobody is ever lost.
11-13.vivre: Give a second chance to someone who has let you down.

11-14: Saint Laurence O'Toole: an Archbishop of Dublin and a peacemaker.

11-14.qui: Laurence O'Toole (1128-1180) was Archbishop of Dublin, in Ireland.
11-14.sens: In a time of war between the Irish and the English, he constantly sought peace. He died at Eu, in Normandy, on his way to plead his people's cause before the King of England, and is buried there.
11-14.vivre: Take a step towards making up after a quarrel.

11-15: Saint Albert the Great: a Dominican scholar, teacher of Saint Thomas Aquinas.

11-15.qui: Albert the Great (c. 1200-1280) was a German Dominican and bishop of Regensburg. He studied everything: plants, animals, minerals, astronomy, philosophy.
11-15.sens: He taught Saint Thomas Aquinas in Paris and Cologne. A Doctor of the Church, he is the patron saint of scientists: for him, studying nature was also a way of admiring its Creator.
11-15.vivre: Look closely at a plant, a stone or an insect, and marvel.

11-16: Saint Margaret of Scotland: a Queen of Scotland, mother of eight, very generous to the poor.

11-16.qui: Margaret (c. 1045-1093), an English princess, became Queen of Scotland when she married King Malcolm. They had eight children.
11-16.sens: Every day she fed poor people at her table, and she founded churches and hostels for pilgrims. She is the patron saint of Scotland. She is celebrated on 16 November, the day of her death.
11-16.vivre: Invite someone who is alone to share a meal.

11-17: Saint Elizabeth of Hungary: a young princess who founded a hospital for the poor.

11-17.qui: Elizabeth of Hungary (1207-1231), daughter of the King of Hungary, married the Landgrave of Thuringia very young. Widowed at 20 with three children, she left the court.
11-17.sens: She devoted the rest of her short life to the sick, in a hospital she founded at Marburg. It is said that bread she was taking to the poor turned into roses. She died at 24.
11-17.vivre: Give a little of your time to a charity that helps the sick or the poor.

11-18: A disciple of Saint Genevieve in Paris.

11-18.qui: Aude was a young woman of the fifth century, a disciple of Saint Genevieve.
11-18.sens: According to tradition, she left her village in Brie to join Genevieve's community in Paris. 18 November is also the Dedication of the Basilicas of Saint Peter and Saint Paul in Rome.
11-18.vivre: Follow the example of someone you admire.

11-19: A Breton monk, founder of the abbey of Saint-Mathieu, near Brest.

11-19.qui: Tanguy was a Breton monk of the sixth century.
11-19.sens: According to tradition, he committed a terrible crime in his youth before converting and founding the abbey of Saint-Mathieu, at the tip of Finistère. He is much loved in Brittany: his story says that God's forgiveness can lift anyone up.
11-19.vivre: Ask forgiveness for a fault that has weighed on you for a long time.

11-20: A young King of East Anglia, martyred in 869.

11-20.qui: Edmund (c. 841-869) was a young King of East Anglia, in England.
11-20.sens: Defeated by Viking invaders, he refused to deny his faith and died a martyr. The town of Bury St Edmunds bears his name; he was long the patron saint of England.
11-20.vivre: Stay true to what you believe, even when it isn't easy.

11-21: Mary, as a child, given to God.

11-21.qui: This day recalls the presentation of the child Mary in the Temple in Jerusalem.
11-21.sens: The story does not come from the Bible but from an ancient text, the Protoevangelium of James. The Church sees in it Mary wholly given to God from childhood. In the East it is one of the great feasts of the year.
11-21.vivre: Offer your day to God, simply, in the morning.

11-22: A Roman martyr, patron saint of musicians.

11-22.qui: Cecilia was a young Roman martyr of the third century, one of the saints honoured from earliest times.
11-22.sens: According to the account of her martyrdom, on her wedding day she “sang to God in her heart” while the instruments played: she became the patron saint of musicians. Choirs and bands all over the world bear her name and celebrate her feast.
11-22.vivre: Sing or listen to a beautiful song, thinking of God.

11-23: Saint Peter's third successor, who wrote a letter to the Christians of Corinth.

11-23.qui: Clement was the third successor of Saint Peter as bishop of Rome, at the end of the first century.
11-23.sens: He wrote a letter to the Christians of Corinth, who were divided by quarrels, calling them to peace and humility: it is one of the oldest Christian texts after the New Testament. According to tradition, he was martyred in Crimea.
11-23.vivre: Write a note to calm a quarrel in your family or among friends.

11-24: Saint Andrew Dung-Lac and 116 companions, killed in the 18th and 19th centuries.

11-24.qui: Andrew Dung-Lac and his 116 companions were martyrs of Vietnam, killed between 1745 and 1862: priests, catechists, mothers and fathers, Vietnamese, Spanish and French.
11-24.sens: Thousands of Christians were persecuted in Vietnam; these were canonized together by John Paul II in 1988. Their faithfulness gave birth to a living Church that is still very active today.
11-24.vivre: Pray for Christians who are persecuted for their faith today.

11-25: Saint Catherine of Alexandria: a learned young woman of Alexandria, patron saint of philosophers.

11-25.qui: According to tradition, Catherine of Alexandria was a very learned young woman in Egypt, martyred early in the fourth century.
11-25.sens: She is said to have stood up to philosophers sent to make her give up her faith, and to have convinced several of them. She is patron saint of philosophers and students; in France her day gave rise to the custom of the “catherinettes”, unmarried women of 25 who wear extravagant hats.
11-25.vivre: Take time to think about a question of faith that is on your mind.

11-26: Saint Innocent of Irkutsk: a Russian missionary, first bishop of Irkutsk in Siberia.

11-26.qui: Innocent Kulchitsky (c. 1680-1731) was an Orthodox monk from Ukraine.
11-26.sens: Sent as a missionary to China, he could not enter and stayed in Siberia, where he became the first bishop of Irkutsk. He is venerated by the Russian Orthodox Church.
11-26.vivre: Pray for the Christians of Russia.

11-27: An icon of Mary that, according to tradition, protected the city of Novgorod in the twelfth century.

11-27.qui: “Our Lady of the Sign” is an icon showing Mary with the child Jesus in a medallion on her breast.
11-27.sens: Its name recalls the sign foretold by Isaiah: a virgin who will bear a son (Is 7:14). According to tradition, in the twelfth century besieged Novgorod, in Russia, was saved after this icon was carried onto the walls. 27 November is also the day of the apparition of the Miraculous Medal in Paris, in 1830.
11-27.vivre: Pray to Mary for a city in danger.

11-28: Saint James of the Marches: a Franciscan preacher who travelled across Eastern Europe.

11-28.qui: James of the Marches (1394-1476) was an Italian Franciscan and a great preacher.
11-28.sens: He travelled through Central Europe and Italy preaching peace and conversion, and helped found the “monti di pietà”, interest-free lending banks to protect the poor from moneylenders.
11-28.vivre: Lend something without expecting anything back.

11-29: The first bishop of Toulouse, Saint Sernin.

11-29.qui: Saturninus, also called Sernin, was the first bishop of Toulouse, in the third century.
11-29.sens: According to tradition, he refused to sacrifice to idols and was tied to a bull that dragged him through the streets of the city. The great Basilica of Saint-Sernin in Toulouse stands over his tomb.
11-29.vivre: Visit an old church in your town and find out who its patron saint is.

11-30: Saint Andrew, apostle: the first one called, Peter's brother.
12-01: King Dagobert's goldsmith, who became bishop of Noyon.

12-01.qui: Eligius (c. 588-660), born in the Limousin, was a goldsmith who became King Dagobert's treasurer.
12-01.sens: He used his fortune to free slaves and found monasteries, then became bishop of Noyon. He is the patron saint of goldsmiths and metalworkers. 1 December is also the feast of Saint Charles de Foucauld.
12-01.vivre: Use your talents in the service of others.

12-02: A young Roman martyr of the fourth century.

12-02.qui: Bibiana, or Viviana, was a young Roman woman martyred under the Emperor Julian, around 363.
12-02.sens: According to tradition, she stayed faithful to her faith despite threats and was beaten to death. A church in Rome bears her name.
12-02.vivre: Pray for young people who keep their faith in spite of everything.

12-03: Saint Francis Xavier: a Navarrese, companion of Ignatius, missionary as far as Japan.

12-03.qui: Francis Xavier (1506-1552), a nobleman of Navarre, was one of Saint Ignatius of Loyola's first companions.
12-03.sens: He went to India, then Japan, and died at the gates of China. Tireless, he baptized thousands of people. He is patron of the missions with Saint Thérèse of Lisieux.
12-03.vivre: Speak simply about your faith to someone who asks.

12-04: A martyr, patron saint of firefighters and miners.

12-04.qui: Barbara was a very popular martyr of the early centuries, whose story is known mainly through legend.
12-04.sens: It is said her father shut her up in a tower and was struck by lightning after killing her. She became the patron saint of all who work with fire and explosives: firefighters, miners, gunners. In Provence, wheat is sown in a saucer on this day so that it will be green by Christmas.
12-04.vivre: Sow a few grains of wheat or lentils in a saucer and watch them grow until Christmas.

12-05: A monk of Moissac who became Archbishop of Braga, in Portugal.

12-05.qui: Gerald (died c. 1108), born in Quercy, was a monk at Moissac.
12-05.sens: The Archbishop of Toledo brought him in to renew liturgical chant; he then became Archbishop of Braga in Portugal, where he rebuilt the Church after Muslim rule.
12-05.vivre: Sing or listen to a beautiful piece of church music.

12-06: The bishop of Myra, protector of children.

12-06.qui: Nicholas was bishop of Myra, in today's Turkey, in the fourth century.
12-06.sens: He is said to have thrown gold secretly through the window of three poor young women so they could marry, and to have saved three children. He became the protector of children. In Belgium, the Netherlands and Germany he brings sweets on the night of 5 to 6 December: Santa Claus comes from him.
12-06.vivre: Give a present in secret, without saying it's from you.

12-07: A bishop of Milan who baptized Saint Augustine.

12-07.qui: Ambrose (c. 340-397) was governor of Milan when, during a stormy election, the people demanded that he become bishop; he was not even baptized yet.
12-07.sens: He became a courageous shepherd who dared stand up to the emperor, and a great preacher: it was by listening to him that Augustine was converted. He composed hymns still sung today. He is celebrated on the day of his ordination as bishop.
12-07.vivre: Listen to or read an ancient hymn of the Church.

12-08: Mary kept free from sin from the first moment of her life.
12-09: Saint Peter Fourier: a parish priest in Lorraine who opened free schools and a mutual aid fund for the poor.

12-09.qui: Peter Fourier (1565-1640) was parish priest of Mattaincourt, in the Vosges.
12-09.sens: He opened free schools for girls with Alix Le Clerc, set up a mutual aid fund so the poor would not fall into debt, and visited every family in his parish. He was called “the good father of Mattaincourt”.
12-09.vivre: Help a child with homework or to learn something.

12-10: Saint Eulalia of Mérida: a 13-year-old martyr, greatly venerated in Spain.

12-10.qui: Eulalia was a girl from Mérida, in Spain, martyred in 304 at about 13.
12-10.sens: The poet Prudentius sang of her courage. She is one of the most venerated martyrs of Spain; she already appears in the sixth-century mosaics of Ravenna. 10 December is also the feast of Our Lady of Loreto.
12-10.vivre: Pray for children who are persecuted.

12-11: A pope who asked Saint Jerome to translate the Bible.

12-11.sens: He asked Saint Jerome to translate the Bible into Latin, the language everyone spoke at the time: the Vulgate. He also had the tombs of the martyrs in the catacombs of Rome found and decorated.
12-11.vivre: Read a Bible passage in your own language, thinking of those who translated it.

12-13: A martyr of Syracuse, whose name means “light”.

12-13.qui: Lucy was a young martyr of Syracuse, in Sicily, around 304.
12-13.sens: Her name comes from the Latin lux, “light”. Her feast once fell on the shortest day of the year: in Sweden it is celebrated with processions of girls crowned with candles, singing in the dark.
12-13.vivre: Light a candle this evening, as a sign of the light that comes at Christmas.

12-14: Saint John of the Cross: a Carmelite of Castile, poet of the night and of love.

12-14.qui: John of the Cross (1542-1591) was a Spanish Carmelite, friend of Saint Teresa of Avila, with whom he reformed the Carmelites.
12-14.sens: Imprisoned by his own brothers, he wrote in his cell some of the most beautiful poems in the Spanish language. He speaks of the “dark night”, those times when God seems absent but is very close. He is a Doctor of the Church.
12-14.vivre: Remember that a hard passage can be a path towards the light.

12-15: Saint Virginia Centurione Bracelli: a widow of Genoa who opened her home to the poor and to orphans.

12-15.qui: Virginia Centurione Bracelli (1587-1651) was a noblewoman of Genoa, widowed at 20 with two daughters.
12-15.sens: During a famine she opened her home to abandoned girls, then founded works for the sick and poor of the city. She was canonized in 2003.
12-15.vivre: Open your door: invite a neighbour or friend round for coffee.

12-16.qui: Adelaide (c. 931-999) was Empress of the Holy Roman Empire.
12-16.sens: Widowed, imprisoned and then freed, she governed wisely, calmed conflicts and founded monasteries. She ended her life in prayer at Seltz, in Alsace.
12-16.vivre: Ease some tension around you with a kind word.

12-17: Today the great “O” Antiphons begin, calling Christ by his names before Christmas.

12-17.qui: From 17 to 23 December the Church sings before the evening Magnificat seven “great antiphons” that all begin with “O”.
12-17.sens: Each calls Christ by a name taken from the Old Testament. The first, “O Wisdom”, asks Christ, the Wisdom that came from the mouth of the Most High, to come and teach us the way. Read backwards, the Latin initials of the seven antiphons spell “ERO CRAS”: “Tomorrow I will be there.”

12-18: The Lord who spoke to Moses in the burning bush, called to come and set us free.

12-18.qui: Adonai is a Hebrew name for God meaning “Lord”.
12-18.sens: The antiphon recalls the burning bush, where God revealed himself to Moses, and the gift of the Law on Sinai: it asks Christ to come and free us “with outstretched arm”, as God freed his people from Egypt.
12-18.vivre: Think of what holds you captive and entrust it to God.

12-19: Christ, descendant of King David, called to come without delay.

12-19.qui: Jesse was the father of King David.
12-19.sens: The prophet Isaiah foretells that “a shoot shall come out from the stump of Jesse” (Is 11:1): a descendant of David, the Messiah. The antiphon sees Jesus as that shoot, before whom kings will fall silent.
12-19.vivre: Look at your family tree and give thanks for those who came before you.

12-20: The one who opens and no one shuts, called to free the captives.

12-20.qui: The key of David is an image from Isaiah (Is 22:22): the one who opens and no one shuts.
12-20.sens: The antiphon asks Christ to come and open the prison and lead out those who sit in darkness.
12-20.vivre: Do something to free someone from a worry or a burden.

12-21: “Radiant Dawn, splendour of eternal light”: Christ, the rising sun.

12-21.qui: 21 December is often the shortest day of the year.
12-21.sens: Today's antiphon calls Christ “Oriens”, the rising star, the sun of justice who comes to shine on those who sit in darkness (Lk 1:78-79). It is also one of the names that inspired Ora.
12-21.vivre: Watch the sunrise if you can, and pray for those who are in darkness.

12-22: Christ, the cornerstone who gathers all peoples together.

12-22.qui: This antiphon calls Christ “King of the nations” and “cornerstone”.
12-22.sens: The cornerstone holds two walls together: Christ gathers all peoples into one. The antiphon asks him to come and save the human being he formed from the earth.
12-22.vivre: Pray for a country at war.

12-23: “God with us”, the last antiphon before Christmas.

12-23.qui: Emmanuel is a Hebrew word meaning “God with us”.
12-23.sens: It is the name foretold by Isaiah (Is 7:14) and taken up in Matthew's Gospel (Mt 1:23). The last antiphon before Christmas sums up all the waiting: God comes to live among us.
12-23.vivre: Remember, at an ordinary moment of the day, that God is with you.

12-24: Tonight the Church keeps watch and waits for the birth of Jesus.

12-24.qui: 24 December is the last day of Advent.
12-24.sens: In the evening the Christmas Eve Mass is celebrated, then Midnight Mass. In many families it is the time for a festive meal, for placing the baby Jesus in the crib, and for presents.
12-24.vivre: Place the baby Jesus in the crib together as a family.

12-25: The birth of Jesus in Bethlehem.
12-26: The first martyr, who forgave those who stoned him.
12-27: Saint John, Apostle and Evangelist: the apostle “whom Jesus loved”.
12-28: The children of Bethlehem killed on Herod's orders.
12-29: On Saint David's day, we think of the shepherd who became king and wrote many psalms.

12-29.qui: David was the youngest son of Jesse, a shepherd of Bethlehem.
12-29.sens: Chosen by God, he defeated Goliath, became King of Israel, and tradition credits him with many psalms. He sinned gravely, then asked forgiveness (Ps 51). Jesus is called “son of David”: he was born in Bethlehem, David's town. 29 December is also the feast of Saint Thomas Becket.
12-29.vivre: Pray a psalm, for example Psalm 23: “The Lord is my shepherd”.

12-30: A very old widow who recognized the child Jesus in the Temple (Lk 2:36-38).

12-30.qui: Anna was a very old prophetess, long widowed, who never left the Temple in Jerusalem.
12-30.sens: When Mary and Joseph presented Jesus in the Temple, she recognized him and spoke of him to all who were waiting for redemption (Lk 2:36-38). A figure of faithfulness and patience.
12-30.vivre: Call an older relative during the holidays.

12-31: The pope of Constantine's time, who closes the year.

12-31.qui: Sylvester was pope from 314 to 335, when the Emperor Constantine ended the persecutions.
12-31.sens: During his pontificate the great basilicas of Rome began to be built. Because he is celebrated on the last day of the year, his name is linked with New Year's Eve in many countries.
12-31.vivre: Thank God for three good things in the year that is ending.
